title: No designed first-run flow or start screen before the first public release
area: first-run: first launch and start screen
description: Walking first launch as a new user: the architecture defines panels, dialogs and install discovery, but no first-launch sequence. There is no install summary with visible defaults, no start screen (Continue / New / Open / Recent / Drill / Sample mission) and no optional 'Coming from' question. The only design is doc 34's research rows le02 and le25. Their owner, I34-33, lands in M4, but M3 (0.5) is the first public release. So first-release users open an empty classic editor with no guided route to a first Preview, and contributors building the M1-M3 shell have no flow to implement or test.
evidence: doc 34 le02, le25 (research proposals, 'adapt'); roadmap/integration-owners.md I34-33 (M4: 'Doc 33 reconciled with le01-le11 ... le25'), the only place le25 appears outside research; m0-m3 M3 goal ('first public release'); ui-shell §6 panel table has no start screen; doc 33 §2 item 5 and §4.8 give only constraints (no start-up tour, at most one dismissible welcome card); 'welcome card' and 'start screen' appear nowhere in architecture/ or decisions/.
frequency: session: every new user once; the start screen every session
removal: Eliminate steps with safe defaults: adopt le25 into ui-shell as M3 work. Auto-detect installs and show them on one summary screen with the defaults already chosen, so no question has to be answered before editing. Add a start screen whose primary action opens a ready-to-Preview sample mission (player placed on a stock island), making the first Preview one click. Keep le02's question optional on the single welcome card (doc 33 principle 5: no start-up tour). Measure time from launch to first Preview (D049 item 3).
change_in: architecture/ui-shell.md (new first-run and start-screen section); roadmap m0-m3 M3 scope; integration-owners I34-33 (split the first-run part out to M3); doc 34 le02/le25 folded
effort: M (UI plus a design note; reuses discovery, staging and templates)

title: Help at the first release: Standing Orders and Drill arrive after M3, and their names do not say 'help'
description: From M2 the dialogs promise that 'greyed-out controls explain their reason with a Standing Orders link', and doc 33 §4.4 promises a 'why' on every disabled control. Standing Orders and Drill track A land in M4 (v1.0 under D036), while M3 has them only 'in draft'. A first-release user who hits a hidden Preview button or a greyed field gets a link to nothing, or no reason at all. The help surfaces also use product names a newcomer will not map to 'manual' or 'tutorial', and doc 09 ranks documentation among the top pain points.
evidence: ui-shell §4 (greyed-out controls link to Standing Orders); architecture README M4 row ('Standing Orders and Drill track A'); m0-m3 M3 lane E ('Standing Orders seed entries in draft; Drill lesson scripts in draft'); D036 item 4; skills/standing-orders (32 seed entries already exist); doc 09 P8, S18; D028 (names).
frequency: session: every session for new users
removal: Automate, then explain at the point of friction. Ship the computed 'why is this greyed or hidden' text in M3, taken from the readiness model and admission (validation-and-lints §13), which needs no manual. Ship the 32 seed entries read-only in a simple pane. Never render a link to a missing entry: CI checks that every anchor a shipped control uses resolves. Pair the names with plain descriptors in menus ('Help: Standing Orders, concept manual'; 'Drill, hands-on tutorials'). Resolve together with FR-P-016 and FR-P-077.
change_in: roadmap M3 scope (lane E); ui-shell §4, §6; doc 33 §4.4; names table (D034; DG037) for the descriptors

title: No default rule or visible summary for which install serves each target profile
description: A typical Steam owner has Remastered PoseidonGame and the legacy ColdWarAssault.exe in the same install, sometimes also GOG, the free demo and a CE build. Doc 08 §5.3 has a situation table, but game-integration §2 has no pure rule that picks the executable for each profile, and nothing shows the result ('Preview uses: Steam Remastered 3.05; 1.99 missions: legacy exe in the same install'). Discovery finds legacy 1.99 only inside the Steam install, so retail or CD 1.99 installs and OFP 1.96 are not covered; those users must use the manual folder, which is [U] for 1.96. The manual picker checks only for PoseidonGame plus DTA/ and Worlds/, so it does not classify legacy layouts.
evidence: game-integration §2; doc 08 §5.2 steps 1-5 (no legacy-retail step; step 4 is the DTA/ plus Worlds/ check), §5.3 table; doc 05 §7.2 ('old and new install side by side'; manual folder 'also covers old OFP 1.96 ... [U]'); doc 27 §4.2.
frequency: once: once per machine; again whenever installs change
removal: Set safe defaults and make wrong input impossible. Add a pure select_default_exe(profile, installs) rule: Steam or GOG Remastered for Cwr, the configured CE build for Ce, the legacy exe in the same install for Cwa199, and never the demo exe. Show its result as one editable line per profile. Make the manual picker classify the chosen folder (Remastered, CE, legacy 1.99, demo data, OFP 1.96 data) and say what each one enables, instead of a pass/fail check. Add detection of retail 1.99 installs as an SP-06 question.
change_in: game-integration §2; doc 08 §5.2 (fold); spikes-and-probes §3.1 (SP-06); plotroom-install tests

title: New missions default to Cwr regardless of which game the user has
description: D003 makes Cwr the default. A user whose only editor-capable install is legacy 1.99 (common in the 1.99 multiplayer community) still creates Cwr missions. The Requires badge says 3.05, editor glue may use Remastered-only constructs, and Preview needs an executable they do not have. They find the mismatch at Preview, or when players cannot load the mission. A user with a CE build must switch every new mission to Ce by hand.
evidence: D003 decision 3 (Cwr default); D003 consequences (file writers default to output every profile accepts, which covers formats but not glue or the badge); validation-and-lints §8; game-integration §2 and §6 (Cwa199 is export-and-open only).
frequency: workflow: every new mission for 1.99-only and CE users
removal: Safe default: preselect the new mission's profile from the installs found (Cwr when a Remastered or CE executable exists, Cwa199 when only legacy 1.99 does) and from the user's last choice, shown as a chip on the New Mission card. The profile stays stored per mission and never global, and capabilities still need UserIntent per mission, so D003's invariants hold. Because this refines D003's 'Default', it needs an owner amendment. Resolve together with FR-P-050.
change_in: D003 (owner amendment note); validation-and-lints §8; ui-shell (New Mission card)

title: Target-profile vocabulary is internal jargon, and there is no answer for OFP 1.96 users
description: Users are asked to choose among Cwa199, Cwr and Ce, a 'target profile', 'capabilities' (which are engine-request ids) and a 'Requires' badge. These are code identifiers; the community says '1.99', 'Remastered' and 'CWR-CE'. The product descriptor names Operation Flashpoint and the readers accept OFP 1.96 files, but no profile tells a 1.96 user where they belong. 'Validate' (the in-game --check run), validation (the Problems panel) and 'Check this install' also overlap.
evidence: D003 table; crate-map (profile ids are owner-decided data values, not product names); validation-and-lints §8 (capabilities are ER-### ids); doc 07 target rule (readers accept OFP 1.96); game-integration §2 ('Check this install') and §6 ('A Validate button runs --check'); ui-shell §6 Settings row.
frequency: workflow: every mission creation and every badge read
removal: Make wrong input impossible through naming, then explain at the point of choice. Put user-facing labels in the names table (for example 'Remastered 3.05 (Steam/GOG)', 'Legacy 1.99', 'Community Edition with extensions'), each with a one-line 'who plays this' and which of the user's installs runs it. Show capabilities by feature name, with ER ids only in the inspector. Give the in-game check a name distinct from validation. D003 defines no 1.96 profile, so which profile 1.96 lands in (proposed: the closest profile, badged 'unverified on 1.96') is a design decision to record as a DG or owner note, not a names-table entry. Resolve together with FR-C-009.
change_in: names table (D034; DG037); ui-shell §6 and §12 (in-app body text); validation-and-lints §8 (badge wording); a DG or owner note for 1.96

title: The first mission has no designed save location, so it may not appear in the game or may fail to save
description: Preview stages to app temp and export writes to the game's missions folders, but no document says where a new mission is saved by default. If the user saves to a Plotroom-chosen folder, the mission does not appear in the game's editor or scenario list until they export it. A legacy install under Program Files can fail on permissions, a known community complaint. The 1.99 missions root depends on the in-game player profile name, which is [U].
evidence: game-integration §5 ('the user's working folder is never launched') and §11 (export); doc 08 §4.1 (export roots); doc 09 P9 ('Saving failed because of folder permissions') and S18 ('clear errors for save location and permissions'); doc 20 OQ10 (1.99 missions root [U]); core-document-model §2, §10, §11 (no default location).
frequency: workflow: once per mission; critical on the first one
removal: Safe default: New Mission saves into the target profile's user missions folder (Documents\Cold War Assault\missions for Cwr and Ce; for Cwa199, the game player profile the user picks from a read-only list of Users\), shown and editable on the New Mission card. The <name>.<Island> folder name is computed, so the user never types the island suffix. Check that the folder is writable before the first save; if it is not, offer the Documents location and say why. The export plan must detect that the project already lives in that missions root, so it does not write a second, diverging copy beside it (doc 08 §4.1 cons). The .plotroom/ sidecar is a dot-directory the CWR exporter skips (1.99 is still [U], SP-08). Preview still stages to temp, so game-integration §5 holds.
change_in: core-document-model §2 and §11 (default location); game-integration §11; ui-shell (New Mission)

title: The first Preview boots the game twice, and a failed probe is cached
description: The capability probe (--version, then a synthetic --check --test-mission run, which is a full game boot) runs on 'Check this install' or on the first Preview, and then the real Preview boots the game again. Boot time is unmeasured. A probe that fails for a transient reason (Steam not running, the game already open) is cached by executable path, size and mtime. Because 'an unknown build counts as lacking every optional capability', later Previews then fall back to export-and-open without saying why.
evidence: game-integration §2 (capability probe resolution) and §14 OQ5; doc 08 §5.2 step 5 and OQ3 (boot time unmeasured); spikes-and-probes §3.1 item 2 (whether Steam must be running is [U]); ER-005 (a rejected path sets no exit code); ER-006 (without --check a failed boot leaves the game at its menu).
frequency: once: once per install, and again after each game update
removal: Eliminate the step: let the first real Preview double as the probe. Run --version, then launch the mission with the P1 flags, and treat the jsonl ready event plus display 46 as proof. Because a rejection sets no exit code (ER-005) and a failed boot without --check leaves the game at its menu (ER-006), 'did not honour the flags' can only be inferred from a missing ready event within a boot budget measured in SP-07. Such an ambiguous result is never cached; it shows 'Re-check'. Only a definitive outcome is cached, and the synthetic --check probe stays for 'Check this install' and the probe suite.
change_in: game-integration §2 and §14 OQ5; m0-m3 M3 exit evidence (fake-binary cases for each probe outcome)

title: Preview launch has no designed progress, timeout or failure states
description: From the click to a running mission the user waits through staging and a boot of unmeasured length, and the design minimises the editor at launch. Several known failures look like 'nothing happened'. Without --check, a failed boot leaves the game running at its menu (ER-006). A rejected path sets no exit code (ER-005). Exit code 2 has several meanings. Steam may have to be running, and the Linux build may need the Steam runtime (both [U]). In strict Preview a script error closes the game. The log panel and the exit-code mapping exist, but no user-facing states, timeouts or next actions are designed.
evidence: ui-shell §12 ('the editor minimises when Preview launches'); game-integration §7 (typed outcomes, log panel); ER-005 and ER-006 ('Plotroom today': a log watch with a timeout); doc 08 §4.2 (exit-code table and caveats) and §7 (risk: AutoTest abort frustrates users); spikes-and-probes §3.1 item 2; display 46 is IDD_MISSION (doc 08).
frequency: constant: every Preview (states); failures occasionally
removal: Explain at the point of friction, with safe defaults. Add a typed Preview status strip in the editor (Staging, Starting game, Loading mission, Running, Ended: <outcome>) driven by jsonl events. Once a boot budget measured in SP-07 passes, it says 'the game is at its menu; the mission did not load (log line N)' and offers Stop. Minimise the editor only when the mission is running (display 46), never on the click. Give each outcome one sentence and one next action, for example 'script error at file:line: open it'. Test every state against the fake game binary.
change_in: game-integration §6-§7; ui-shell §6 (Preview log) and §12 (minimise rule); m0-m3 M3 exit evidence item 2

title: Pressing Preview while a Preview is running is undefined
description: Each edit-then-Preview cycle relaunches the game, because hot reload needs ER-003. If the previous Preview is still running, the design does not say whether Preview is disabled, starts a second game, or replaces the first. So the user switches to the game, quits it, comes back and clicks again, many times per session.
evidence: doc 08 §4.4 ('Hot reload ... Relaunch instead (boot cost unmeasured)'); ER-003 (not filed); game-integration §7-§8 (supervisor and Stop verb exist; P1 includes --harness 0, with kill_on_drop and a Job Object as fallback); ui-shell §6; no design for 'already running' or a second instance exists in docs/.
frequency: constant: many times per session
removal: Eliminate the step: while a supervised Preview runs, the Preview button becomes 'Restart Preview'. One click stops the game (harness exit, then kill after a timeout), restages the current snapshot and relaunches. Two games never run at once, and Stop stays one keypress away in the editor. Restart is an explicit user click, so UserIntent still gates each launch.
change_in: game-integration §7; ui-shell §6

title: Shift+Preview (briefing first) cannot work in strict Preview, and nothing replaces it
area: first-run: Preview and the first briefing
description: Doc 09 lists Shift+Preview, which shows the briefing first, as a must-keep. --test-mission never shows the briefing, and the fix is ER-001's --preview-briefing (CE first, Cwr only if ported, 1.99 never). A first-time author writes a briefing and has no way to see it through Preview, and the design does not say what Shift+Preview does in the meantime.
evidence: doc 09 M8 (must keep: 'Shift+Preview shows the briefing'); doc 08 §4.2 caveats ('There is no briefing'); ER-001; game-integration §6 (P3 row, Ce opt-in only).
frequency: workflow: every briefing iteration
removal: Explain at the point of friction and automate what exists. Shift+Preview first opens an in-editor briefing view rendered from the briefing CST (plotroom-briefing) with the mission's markers, labelled 'editor rendering; the game shows it only on CE with ER-001', then launches. The rendering stays labelled as an approximation, because D018 rejects in-editor simulation as a source of truth. Once the Ce capability is probed, Shift+Preview passes --preview-briefing. The shortcut never silently does the same thing as plain Preview.
change_in: game-integration §6; ui-shell §6 (briefing view); M2/M3 parity script for doc 09 M8

title: Long staging paths make Preview fail silently (ER-004)
description: The engine re-stages the test mission to <TempDir>/mission-smoke/<16 hex>/Missions/<name>.<island>/mission.sqm, in a buffer declared as 256 bytes. TempDir defaults to %TEMP%\cwr, which contains the user name. A long user name, a long temp root or a long mission name truncates the path and nothing starts. Plotroom's current mitigation is to 'keep staging roots and mission folder names short', which the user can neither see nor control, and Plotroom's own staging root does not appear in the truncated path at all.
evidence: ER-004 ('Plotroom today' column); game-integration §5 (stage path <app temp>/preview/<session>/<name>.<World>/); doc 01 §7.2 (POSEIDON_TEMP_DIR); doc 08 §2.4 A.1.
frequency: once: rare, but a silent failure when it happens
removal: Make wrong input impossible: in pre-flight, compute the engine's re-staged path, <engine TempDir>/mission-smoke/<16 hex>/Missions/<stem>.<island>/mission.sqm. If it would exceed 255 bytes, the LaunchSpec builder sets POSEIDON_TEMP_DIR to a short Plotroom-owned folder (doc 01 §7.2; whether shipping builds honour it is a P0/SP-07 question). Shorten the staged stem only as a last resort, and say so in the Preview status. Test at 255 and 256 bytes.
change_in: game-integration §5; ER-004 row ('Plotroom today'); spikes-and-probes SP-07

title: macOS, Linux arm64 and demo-only users must hand-install a CE build before any Preview
description: macOS and Linux arm64 have no official editor-capable executable, and the free demo's executable has no editor module. Preview therefore needs a CE build that the user fetches from CI artifacts (which expire), copies into the Remastered or demo folder (CE binaries are 'not drop-in compatible with original game folder') and then points Plotroom at. The README's 'What you need' says only 'your own copy of the game (Steam or GOG)'. Plotroom cannot fetch the build: game executables are not a D008 source kind.
evidence: D018 decision 1; doc 08 §5.1 (CE row) and §5.3 table (demo-only row); D003 alternatives ('CE build artifacts expire'); README 'What you need'; spikes-and-probes §3.1 item 3.
frequency: once: once per machine (a blocker for these users)
removal: Explain at the point of friction, because removal needs a download source. The install summary says per OS what works ('Editing: yes, from your demo data. Preview: needs a full-game executable; CE build steps'), with a link opened only on the user's click. The executable picker checks the chosen file with --version and explains any mismatch. The README gets a per-OS, per-install table. Record a candidate DG: a D008 user-enabled source for pinned, hash-checked CE builds (owner decision; executable downloads raise security questions).
change_in: README.md; game-integration §2; ui-shell first-run summary; a new DG for CE-build downloads

title: Every 1.99 Preview costs 5-7 manual clicks in the game
description: Cwa199 missions get only export-and-open. Each iteration means export, launch the legacy exe, then Open Editor, select island, Load, name, Preview inside the game. If the user saves inside the game, the exported copy diverges from the project. This is the only Preview path for the still-active 1.99 multiplayer community.
evidence: doc 08 §4 option table (row 1: about 5-7 steps) and §4.1 (already proposes the overwritten export folder and the timestamp warning); game-integration §6 ('the only path for Cwa199'); doc 08 OQ6 (positional mission.sqm and -name= syntax on 1.99 [U]); spikes-and-probes SP-07 item 6 and SP-08.
frequency: constant: every Preview for 1.99 authors
removal: Automate what the engine allows, then explain the rest at the point of friction. If SP-08 shows that 1.99 accepts a positional mission.sqm, launch straight into the mission. Otherwise launch with the right player profile (-name=, if SP-08 confirms the syntax), copy the mission name to the clipboard, and show the remaining in-game clicks as a short checklist. Keep one fixed, overwritten export folder and flag in-game saves by timestamp, as doc 08 §4.1 already proposes.
change_in: game-integration §6; spikes-and-probes SP-08 (question order)

title: Missions that need mods leave the user to assemble mod sets by hand
description: Opening a downloaded mission whose addOns[] names installed mods shows a banner, 'Pick a mod set that has them'. First run offers only one-mod sets, and 'Plotroom invents no combinations', so a user with @CSLA and @WGL installed must build and order a two-mod set before the mission shows its units. After 'Launch the game to install mods' and the rescan on focus, nothing says the pending missing-mod card turns into 'Add X to this mission's set'.
evidence: doc 27 §4.11 ('Pick a mod set that has them') and §4.2; doc 42 §4.2 ('Plotroom invents no combinations', because no channel publishes dependencies) and §4.3 step 3; D038 item 1 (rescan on focus); game-integration §3 (mount order decides which class wins).
frequency: workflow: every downloaded or mod-dependent mission
removal: Automate: compute the covering set from installed mods whose CfgPatches cover the mission's addOns[], ordered by requiredAddons (a fact derived from the mission's own declaration, not an invented combination), and offer it as one labelled button, 'Use @CSLA + @WGL (both installed)', with a line saying what it changes. Where two covering mods define the same class and requiredAddons does not order them, show that choice rather than picking an order, because mount order decides which class wins. After a rescan, pending missing-mod cards resolve themselves and offer the same one-click add. Addons still uncovered stay ghost entities with the three routes. Nothing is downloaded (D030).
change_in: doc 27 §4.11; doc 42 §4.2-§4.3; game-integration §3

title: Easy mode hides fields that hold non-default values, and nothing says so
description: Easy hides what the original editor hides (D029). Advanced is the default, so this affects users who choose Easy or get it through the le02 first-run question. A user in Easy who opens a mission of their own, a downloaded one or an AI-generated one may meet behaviour driven by a hidden field that is set (presence condition, placement radius, init line), with no sign of it. Finding the field means switching modes by trial and error. For AI-set values this also weakens the glass box's 'easy to see'.
evidence: D029 decision 1 (Advanced default); doc 33 §1.2 row 19 ('Easy only hides things'); ui-shell §4; AGENTS.md glass-box invariant ('easy to see').
frequency: session: every dialog opened in Easy on an existing mission (Easy users)
removal: Explain at the point of friction: in Easy, a dialog with hidden non-default fields shows '2 hidden settings are set: Presence condition, Init', with a one-click reveal of just those rows; Easy otherwise stays Easy. The inspector badges the entity. Add a test per preset that every hidden non-default field is announced.
change_in: ui-shell §4; D029 consequences (proposal note); doc 33 lesson C7

title: F1 selects Units mode, not Help, and the docs disagree about F1 help
area: first-run: keyboard map and help discoverability
description: The Classic keymap, the default, keeps F1 as Units mode, so help lives on hover 'More', '?' or 'What is this?'. A newcomer presses F1 for help and silently changes mode. D028's consequences still promise 'F1 pages' and doc 33 §4.4 promises answers 'on hover and F1', contradicting ui-shell §6 and doc 34 le06. '?' also sits on different keys across layouts.
evidence: ui-shell §6 (Standing Orders row: 'F1 only where F1 is not a mode key'); doc 34 le06 (F1 stays Units; {action:...} tokens); D028 consequences ('hover cards, F1 pages'); doc 33 §4.4; doc 09 S18 (asks for an F1 shortcut overlay).
frequency: session: every new user; contributors on every help-related change
removal: Explain at the point of friction, and remove the contradiction. Add a small, permanent status-bar hint generated from the active keymap ('Help: ? or hover · F1-F6: modes'; le07's overlay, adopted). Bind help as a semantic action with its key shown per layout. Reword D028 and doc 33 to 'the help action (F1 where F1 is free)'; the D028 change needs an amendment note. Contributor rule: help text uses {action:help} tokens, never literal keys. Resolve together with FR-P-054, FR-P-017 and FR-P-002.
change_in: D028 (owner amendment note on wording); doc 33 §4.4 (fold); ui-shell §8; doc 34 le07 adoption

title: The Classic keymap assumes a desktop keyboard, and mode keys fail silently without map focus
description: F1-F6 modes, keypad zoom and keypad 5 (centre on player) are faithful to the original. On most laptops, though, F-keys are media keys that need Fn, there is no keypad, and macOS binds several F-keys to the system. Mode keys also work only while the classic view has focus: F2 pressed while the outliner is focused does nothing and says nothing.
evidence: ui-shell §3 (map hotkeys only while the classic view has focus; doc 06 §4.5) and §8 (Classic is the default; the per-OS clash test covers app shortcuts, not Fn or keypad availability); doc 34 le06 (keypad 5) and le07 (pinned mode strip); m0-m3 M2 parity scripts ('keypad and wheel zoom').
frequency: session: every session for laptop and macOS users
removal: Safe defaults, then explain at the point of friction. Keep the pinned mode strip (le07) always visible and ship keypad-free alternates in the Classic profile (for example +/- to zoom and Home to centre on the player, and number-row alternates for modes where those keys are free). When a mode key arrives while another panel has focus, do not reroute keys that panels use themselves (F2 is 'rename' in many trees and outliners); show a transient 'mode keys act on the map (click the map or press <focus-map key>)' hint instead, and route only keys the focused panel does not bind. Cover this with the per-OS clash test and a no-keypad keyboard profile test. Resolve together with FR-P-016.
change_in: ui-shell §3 and §8; doc 34 le06/le07 (fold); M2 parity scripts

title: Plotroom has no designed update path, and game updates trigger unexplained re-probes
description: D008 lists every allowed outbound destination, and an update check is not among them, so users learn about new releases only from outside the app. Doc 34 le07's 'What changed' cards are marked adopt but not yet folded (I34-MERGE pending), and the Model Manager's manifest changes only with releases. After a Steam patch the cached capability probe is invalidated by size and mtime, and the next Preview waits for a re-probe with no reason shown.
evidence: D008 decision 1; no update-check or updater design exists in docs/; doc 34 le07 (adopt, not folded); agent-runtime §13 (manifest updates between releases are a proposal); game-integration §2 (probe cache key).
frequency: once: every release; every game patch
removal: Safe default plus explanation at the point of friction. Add an opt-in 'Check for Plotroom updates' source under D008: off by default, blocked offline, signature- or hash-checked, and ending in either a link or a download the user starts. Offer it once on the welcome card. After an update, show a 'What changed' card built from a versioned changelog (le07). When the game executable has changed, the Preview status says 'Game updated: checking what this build supports (once)'. Downloading Plotroom binaries is a new source kind and needs the owner.
change_in: D008 (owner decision on an update-check source); ui-shell; game-integration §2

title: Network state is hard to see, and offline local AI needs the network first
description: Sources are off by default, and a separate offline mode also blocks the enabled ones. A single list of enabled sources is still only a proposal. When offline mode is on and Wilco is bound to a cloud provider, the design says only that non-loopback backends are blocked. For offline or air-gapped users, the local route needs two downloads (the managed server binary and a GGUF) and has no 'import from file' path, even when the user already has the GGUF from another tool.
evidence: D008 decision 2 and consequences ('one settings list is a proposal'); agent-runtime §3 ('Offline mode blocks every non-loopback backend') and §13 (server binary and GGUF are both downloads); D022 item 4; no import-from-file design exists in docs/.
frequency: session: every session (state); rarely (offline setup)
removal: Explain at the point of friction and eliminate a step. Add one always-visible network chip ('Offline' or '2 sources on') that opens the source list. When offline mode blocks Wilco's bound provider, Wilco's panel says so and offers the local or no-AI route. Add 'Import model file...' and 'Import server build...' through a file dialog the user drives, verifying against the manifest SHA-256 (qualified) or installing as custom and unqualified (D037), with no network use. A user-driven import is a product import flow AGENTS.md allows.
change_in: D008 consequences; agent-runtime §3 and §13; ui-shell §6 (Settings)

title: Models cannot read the environment state they are asked about
area: first-run: setup questions via Wilco and external agents
description: Users will ask Wilco setup questions: 'why is Preview greyed?', 'which game versions do I have?', 'which mods does this mission need?'. Wilco's reach is Query, Lookup, Propose, Check and Ask over documents and references plus Preview run reports. Installs, per-profile capability results, mod-set resolution, offline state and readiness are not listed as queryable, and the MCP surface is generated from the command registry and MissionQuery only. A model must either guess, and install or version facts are easy to hallucinate, or send the user off to look.
evidence: agent-runtime §2 (AgentTool and AgentEffect; reads run reports only); extensibility §10 (MCP tools from the registry plus MissionQuery); validation-and-lints §11 (Wilco may only phrase computed readiness items); doc 21 §11.1.
frequency: workflow: every setup question
removal: Automate: add one read-only typed query, environment.status, as a QueryOp over product state (not a new AgentTool variant). It returns installs by kind and version, the executable serving each profile, probed capabilities with their date, mod-set resolution and missing addons, offline mode, the last Preview outcome and the readiness items. Paths are reduced to kinds, so no user names leak (as the sidecar rule in agent-runtime §3). Wilco and MCP clients can both reach it. A small fixed schema means one cheap call answers the question.
change_in: agent-runtime §2; extensibility §10; the command registry (a query op)

title: Connecting an external agent over MCP has no designed setup, and no way to hand over the address and token
description: The MCP server ships in v1 (opt-in, loopback only, token-authenticated), but no flow says how a user enables it, finds the port and token, or configures a client such as Claude Code or Codex. Doc 15 suggests 'a per-session token', which would mean pasting a new configuration every session. Doc 38 §9 defers a portable bundle of the skill plus MCP configuration. Nothing tells the external agent that its runs wait for a click in the editor, so it may poll or retry. Merged from a duplicate finding about how external agents receive the server address and token.
evidence: extensibility §10; D036 item 6; agent-runtime §15; doc 38 §9 (a portable bundle 'possible later'); doc 15 §7 item 10 ('require a per-session token'); crate-map (plotroom-mcp).
frequency: once: once per client setup; again after every token rotation
removal: Eliminate steps and explain at the point of friction. Add a 'Connect an external agent' panel that starts the server on click and shows the endpoint, a ready configuration snippet per named client copied with one click, and the connected clients. Use a persistent, revocable token kept in the OS keychain and a stable loopback port instead of a per-session token; 'Revoke' rotates the token. Plotroom writes nothing into other programs' configuration files. workflow.start returns a typed awaiting_editor_approval status with a hint, so agents stop retrying (model-side status design: FR-M-002). Resolve together with FR-P-081.
change_in: extensibility §10; doc 38 §9; crate-map (plotroom-mcp)

title: Preview and install behaviour can be verified only on the owner's hardware, and the results live in prose
description: SP-06, SP-07 and SP-08 run on the owner's real installs. Their answers go into doc 08's verification notes and game-integration §14, and the fake game binary and discovery fixtures are hand-written 'to match'. Contributors without the game, and CI, cannot reproduce a real launch trace, and after a game patch there is nothing to diff against. probe-results.csv is only a proposal, created with the first result.
evidence: spikes-and-probes §2 table (SP-06 and SP-07: 'Owner's real installs'), §3.1-§3.2 exits and §4.3 (probe-results.csv proposal); m0-m3 M3 exit evidence item 2 (fake game binary); AGENTS.md fixture rules.
frequency: workflow: every change in the Preview or install area
removal: Automate: add a probe --record mode that captures each real launch of a synthetic mission as a redacted trace fixture (argv shape, exit code, jsonl events, timings; user names and paths stripped). Traces hold only event shapes, codes and timings, never game data, and a hygiene test checks each committed trace. The fake game binary replays them. Record results as rows in probe-results.csv, created now with just its header.
change_in: spikes-and-probes §3 and §4.3; architecture/testing-strategy.md (fake game binary); game-integration §7

title: DG001's file is unnumbered, and the docs index warns about it instead of fixing it
description: The Preview design gap that this whole area cites as DG001 lives in DG-preview-non-aborting-launch.md, whose header still says 'ID: not yet numbered'. docs/README lists it under 'Watch for'. A coding agent that searches for a file named DG001 does not find it, which wastes a lookup on every Preview-console question. The DG README already defers the rename to a change that also updates doc 08 §4.4.
evidence: docs/design-gap-requests/DG-preview-non-aborting-launch.md (header); docs/README §2.2, DGnnn row ('DG001's file is still DG-preview-non-aborting-launch.md'); DG README naming note.
frequency: workflow: every DG001 lookup
removal: Eliminate the step: rename the file to DG001-preview-non-aborting-launch.md, set its ID line and update the links (doc 08 §4.4, game-integration, the roadmap) in one change set, then drop the 'Watch for' note.
change_in: docs/design-gap-requests/ (rename); docs/README §2.2; links in doc 08, game-integration and the roadmap

title: The 'On this PC' path may have no recommended model at v1
description: D037 lets the recommended list hold only models that 'passed Plotroom's own qualification', but the evidence the design plans to have stops at 'spike-checked'. Agent-runtime §7 says badges read 'spike-checked' until doc 21 §12.3's product qualification exists. M6 exit evidence item 7 asks only for 'spike-checked' badges. Doc 55 §3.4 reserves 'qualified' for consecutive all-pass trials. Both provisional 8 GB defaults are still candidates (D023 amendment). Gemma 4 E4B QAT is blocked by its licence-tag mismatch, and CPU-only machines have no verdict (doc 49). If nothing is 'qualified' at release, every local user takes the 'custom' path: licence text to accept, an 'unqualified' badge, and reduced shapes. Fill is offered only as a pre-fill confirmed each time, and Compose and Draft are unavailable.
evidence: D037 decisions 1-2; agent-runtime §7 and §13; roadmap m4-v1 M6 exit evidence item 7 ('shown as spike-checked badges'); doc 55 §3.4; D023 amendment note of 2026-09-27 (both defaults stay candidates; Gemma licence-tag mismatch); doc 49 TL;DR (CPU-only: no verdict).
frequency: once: once per install, on every local user's first path
removal: Safe default: make doc 21 §12.3's product qualification, or a bar the owner names, a v1.0 release gate, so that when M6 ships at least one OSI-licensed model is recommendable per reference hardware class (8 GB GPU, iGPU laptop, and CPU-only or an explicit 'no local model for this PC yet'). Raise M6 exit item 7 from 'spike-checked' to that bar. Fallback: file a DG so the gap is decided rather than discovered at release (whether spike-checked satisfies D037 decision 1 is genuinely ambiguous). Either 'spike-checked' becomes recommendable under that label, or the local card says in plain words that no model is recommended yet and why. Resolve together with FR-P-064 and FR-P-023.
change_in: D037 (which badge state satisfies decision 1); roadmap m4-v1 M6 exit evidence item 7; agent-runtime §7, §13; doc 21 §12.3; a new DG
effort: L for the product-qualification protocol plus runs on three reference machines; S for the DG alone

title: After connecting a model, every role is still 'unassigned'
description: D024 item 4 has the user bind each of six roles (router, writer, scripter, explainer, play-tester, translator) to a configured model. An unbound role shows 'unassigned' and its steps follow their failure route. Neither the connect flow (doc 50 §4) nor the Model Manager (agent-runtime §13) binds anything. The plan card shows bindings, but 'Role bindings are shown and changed only in Settings' (doc 38 §5.2). Free text in chat goes through IntentFill then Dispatch, which is a model step [I], so a user who connected a model and bound only the writer may get no chat at all. The first run after connecting is likely to meet 'unassigned' and a detour to Settings, Roles.
evidence: D024 item 4; doc 21 §7.2; doc 38 §5.2 ('shown and changed only in Settings'); agent-runtime §9 (IntentFill, Dispatch), §11 ('set explicitly in Settings'); doc 50 §4 has no binding step; no default-binding rule exists in docs/.
frequency: once: once per setup and again for each new setup; blocks the first run until found
removal: Safe default: the connect-success card proposes a complete binding computed from what the new setup is qualified or allowed for, for example 'Use Qwen3.5-4B for router and explainer; writer: template text until you add a writer'. One click accepts it. This is still an explicit user binding (D024 item 4 holds), and every plan card shows it. Eliminate step: let the plan card bind an 'unassigned' role inline, with the same control Settings uses, instead of sending the user away (this changes doc 38 §5.2's Settings-only rule). Resolve together with FR-P-065.
change_in: D024 item 4 (a note); doc 38 §5.2; doc 50 §4 (a new step after connecting); agent-runtime §11; ui-shell Settings row

title: The free-cloud option can lead to nothing, at release and between releases
description: D045 item 4 offers a free model only for the step kinds it is qualified for. Item 7 fixes the preset list at release, after the legal review and the providers' written answers. Doc 52 notes that no free cloud model is qualified for any step kind yet, then says the free path 'stays custom, unqualified', which item 4 does not allow. After release, free offers churn (at least five were cut in 2026, doc 50 §2.5). The privacy default admits one free generalist (doc 50 §4 step 7). When it disappears, every call returns the guardrail 404 that doc 52 §5.2 classes as 'a setup fault, shown to the user'. D045 item 6's fallback, 'another offered model qualified for that step kind', needs qualified replacements. Qualification data changes only with releases unless the user has found and enabled the manifest update source (agent-runtime §13 proposal).
evidence: D045 items 4, 6, 7; doc 52 TL;DR ('any free cloud model offered today, because none is qualified per step kind yet') and §6.1 D045 item 5; doc 50 §2.5, §4 step 7; doc 52 §5.2 (LimitOutcome::NoEndpointForPolicy, ModelGone); agent-runtime §13 (update source is a proposal, off by default).
frequency: once: once per setup; again each time a free offer changes
removal: Eliminate step: show the 'Free cloud model with your own account' card only when the release, or an update the user accepted, carries at least one qualified free preset for the step kinds it would be bound to. Do not show an option that leads nowhere. Automate: at session start, the catalogue read that doc 50 §4 step 6 already allows checks that a qualified, policy-compatible free endpoint still exists. If none does, D045 item 6's choice card appears once, before any call, instead of a 404 on every call. Explain at point of friction: that card offers a one-click 'Plotroom model data' update source (user-enabled and hash-checked, per D008) beside local, own key and no AI. D050 (accepted 2026-09-28, after this row was written) reads free cloud as custom and unqualified until qualification runs (Consequences), moves past a removed free model as a limit outcome (item 3) and has the free flow lead to two providers plus a local model (item 2); showing the free card only when a qualified preset exists would now change D050 item 2, so it needs the owner. Resolve together with FR-P-021.
change_in: D045 (reconcile item 4 with doc 52 §6.1 item 5); doc 50 §4 steps 6-8; agent-runtime §13; doc 52 §5.2

title: The first choice asks users what their PC can run, though the product can measure it
description: Doc 50 §4 step 0 opens with three equal cards and 'Nothing is preselected'. Hardware detection happens only inside the Model Manager, after the user picks 'On this PC'. A user with a CPU-only laptop can walk into the Model Manager and find nothing, because doc 49 leaves CPU-only machines at 'No AI or bring-your-own' until a CPU row passes. A user with an 8 GB GPU may pick cloud without knowing that a free, offline, limit-free option fits. Fit badges also use free VRAM 'as measured now' (doc 44 §5.3), so the same PC gets different recommendations depending on what else is open; in doc 44 the desktop alone used 2,700 of 8,192 MiB.
evidence: doc 50 §4 step 0; doc 44 §5.3 (hardware first; Fits = measured increase + 512 MiB <= free VRAM now); doc 49 TL;DR and §5.2 (T1-cpu row: unmeasured, No AI or bring-your-own); doc 52 §6.1 D022 item ('no limits, no account'); agent-runtime §13.
frequency: once: once per setup
removal: Automate: run the local hardware probe (no network, so D004 and D008 are untouched) before drawing the three cards, and annotate each card with its computed outcome for this PC, for example 'Your 8 GB GPU: runs a 2.3 GB model, no account, no limits' or 'No local model is recommended for this PC yet'. The cards can stay unselected if neutrality is wanted. Safe default: compute fit from total VRAM minus a measured desktop baseline. Show the current free VRAM only as a note ('close other GPU apps for more headroom'); the recheck at load time is required, because a baseline-based fit can overpromise.
change_in: doc 50 §4 step 0; doc 44 §5.3 fit rule; agent-runtime §13; ui-shell Settings row

title: Local setup is several separate downloads behind a source switch
description: Getting a local model takes several steps, each started by the user. First, enable Hugging Face as a download source (D008: every source is off by default). Then download the managed llama-server build, a separate pinned download (agent-runtime §13), and the GGUF (about 2.3 GiB). On NVIDIA cards, decide on an optional CUDA build: 645 MB plus cudart, against 32 MB (doc 49 §5.1). Possibly add an opt-in heavy-step model, and for a gated repository supply the user's own Hugging Face token (doc 44 §5.3). Where the source switch lives is itself only a proposal (D008 Consequences). That is an estimated 8-12 clicks and two trips between screens before the first call [I].
evidence: D008 items 1-2 and Consequences; D022 item 4 and amendment items 2-3; agent-runtime §13 ('the managed server's own binary is a pinned, hash-checked download under the same rules'); roadmap M6 ('downloads started only by the user from an enabled source'); doc 49 §5.1-§5.2; doc 44 §5.3 (gated repositories need the user's token).
frequency: once: once per setup; again for each extra model or runtime variant
removal: Eliminate step: one 'Set up on this PC' card lists every component: the runtime build and its size, the model file and its size, the origins (huggingface.co and the runtime's release host) and the licences. A single user click enables exactly those named sources for those pinned files and starts the resumable, hash-checked downloads. D008 still holds: the user starts it, the origins are shown, it is blocked offline, and Wilco can never start it. This reading of D008 needs an owner note. Safe default: preselect the runtime variant measured best for the detected GPU (CUDA on NVIDIA once doc 49's proposal is adopted), showing its extra size and the one-time kernel wait. Prefer ungated repositories for recommended files, so no account is needed.
change_in: D008 (a note that a click on a named-origin download is the enabling gesture); agent-runtime §13; doc 44 §5.3; roadmap m4-v1 M6

title: Users cannot tell what a model setup will actually do
description: Badges per step kind and per setup are honest, but their states multiply. Doc 55 §3.4 has spike-checked, qualified, not-met and requalifying; §3.5 adds 'custom: unqualified' and 'untested on this file'. Doc 44 §5.3 has 'With cards', 'Fields: side, time, archetype', 'Candidates', 'No; cards are shown instead' and 'local check, n = 30 menus'. Doc 50 §6 adds 'screened in the cloud'. On top come the fit badges (Fits, Tight, Partial offload, CPU only) and doc 63 §7's ladder grid of level by DecisionKind family. The step-kind names PICK, FILL, COMPOSE, DRAFT and EXPLAIN are internal words. Free models are offered per step kind (D045 item 4), so a user who connects 'a free model' may expect briefings and get template text. Badge wording is still open (doc 21 OQ3).
evidence: doc 55 §3.4-§3.5; doc 44 §5.3; doc 50 §6; doc 63 §7; agent-runtime §7, §13; D045 item 4; D022 Open parts (doc 21 OQ3, badge wording).
frequency: session: every visit to the Model Manager or the connect flow; the plan card every run
removal: Explain at point of friction, with computed text: every Model Manager row, connect card and plan card starts with one code-built sentence saying what this setup will do in this editor and what falls back to what, for example 'Will: choose options, fill mission fields. Not yet: write briefings; those use template text.' Safe default: users see three states (Checked, Not checked, Checking), mapped from the internal ones. The per-step grid, evidence links and fit numbers sit behind 'Details'. This is not a single score (doc 21 §12.3 forbids one), and the full detail stays one click away. Resolve together with FR-P-075.
change_in: doc 21 OQ3 (badge wording); doc 44 §5.3; doc 55 §3.4-§3.6; doc 63 §7; agent-runtime §7, §13

title: Existing Ollama or LM Studio users start with every Fill asking for confirmation
description: Ollama and LM Studio are auto-detected (agent-runtime §3). Badges belong to the exact setup, so a bring-your-own endpoint shows 'unqualified' until qualification passes on it (D037 Consequences), even when it serves the very file the manifest recommends. With no record, Pick runs with cards, Fill is offered 'only as a pre-fill the user confirms', and Compose and Draft are unavailable (agent-runtime §7). The fix, 'Check this model on my machine', is a separate action of about 300 calls and 4-8 minutes (doc 44 §5.3). Yet doc 55 §4.5 already treats a runtime or backend change on the same file as minor, needing only a quick re-check.
evidence: agent-runtime §3 (auto-detected), §7 (setups without a record); D037 Consequences (a bring-your-own endpoint stays unqualified until checked on that endpoint); doc 44 §5.3 (about 300 calls, 4-8 min); doc 55 §4.5 (llama.cpp build or backend: minor, quick re-check).
frequency: session: every session until the user runs a check
removal: Automate: when the detected endpoint's model file hash matches a manifest entry, treat it as doc 55 §4.5's runtime change (minor, 'requalifying'; needs a D037 note). Offer the quick check (must-pass items plus 30 held-out menus) on the detection card. For other models, offer 'Check now (about N min, runs on this PC, no network)', pre-ticked on the install or detection card. No grant is raised before the quick check passes. Until it passes, the plan card says in one line why Fill will ask for confirmation. Whether Ollama exposes the GGUF's SHA-256 through its blob digests needs a spike [I].
change_in: D037 Consequences; doc 55 §4.5; agent-runtime §7, §13; DG012

title: Local model loads are long waits with no designed feedback or warm-up, and the model is unloaded before every Preview
description: The sidecar starts on demand: it waits for /health, reads /props and makes a warm-up call (agent-runtime §3). To free VRAM, the local model is unloaded or the managed server paused before every Preview launch, even on machines with enough memory, and reloading costs 6-18 s warm or about 33 s cold (doc 44 §5.3). Swapping to the heavy-step offload model costs 7-9 s plus about 12 s for its first call (doc 49 §5.2). A CUDA build adds a one-time kernel compile of 38-105 s per model on older cards (doc 49 §5.1). Only the CUDA wait has a proposed label ('preparing GPU kernels'). Every one of these waits lands on the first interactive request, far beyond doc 53's 1-2 s class for Picks and beyond doc 52's 10-s stall threshold (UX2). Merged from a duplicate finding about the unload before Preview.
evidence: agent-runtime §3 (sidecar start-up), §13 (unload before Preview); game-integration §6 ('The local model is unloaded, or the managed server paused, before the game launches'); doc 44 §5.3 (6-18 s warm, about 33 s cold); doc 49 §5.1 (38-105 s kernel compile), §5.2 (swap cost); doc 52 §4 UX1-UX2; spikes-and-probes §5 item 9 (cold loads and swaps unmeasured).
frequency: constant: every session start and after every Preview, for local-model users
removal: Automate: start and warm the chosen local model when the Wilco panel or a plan card that needs a model opens, and reload it in the background as soon as the game exits after Preview, with a visible 'Wilco reloading' chip. Safe default: unload before Preview only when the model's measured memory fit (the Model Manager's rows) plus the game's measured footprint exceeds free VRAM, and otherwise keep the model loaded; a setting overrides the rule, and cloud backends are untouched. This is local only, uses the model the user already chose, and makes no network call. Point the CUDA kernel cache at Plotroom's data folder, as doc 49 proposes. Explain at point of friction: a status-bar line shows the phase and an estimate ('Loading Qwen3.5-4B... about 15 s'), and the plan card's time estimate includes any pending load.
change_in: agent-runtime §3, §13; game-integration §6; doc 44 §5.3; doc 49 §5.1; ui-shell status bar; SP-13 (measure the game's VRAM footprint and model reload times)

title: Setup lives in Settings, away from the places users reach for AI
description: With Wilco off by default, 'Settings and the Model Manager offer setup' (agent-runtime §1), and the connect flow starts at Settings, Wilco, 'Connect a model' (doc 50 §4 step 0). Users meet AI elsewhere: in the Wilco panel, on the plan card (which always shows the $0 template alternative), at the campaign flow's intake and in idea cards. From each of those places the user is sent to Settings and back, and loses their place in the run they wanted [I].
evidence: agent-runtime §1 ('Settings and the Model Manager offer setup'); doc 50 §4 step 0; doc 40 §6 and agent-runtime §12 ($0 alternative on the plan card); ui-shell Wilco and Settings rows.
frequency: once: once per setup; on every AI entry point until connected
removal: Eliminate step: show the same connect cards inline at each AI entry point: the Wilco panel's empty state, a plan card with no model (beside its $0 template option) and the campaign flow's intake. Finishing them returns the user to the waiting run. Settings stays the full view. Nothing is sent before the user's gesture (D004, D008), and Wilco still cannot start the flow (doc 50 §4).
change_in: agent-runtime §1; doc 50 §4 step 0; doc 38 §5.2; ui-shell Wilco and Settings rows

title: The connect flow ends at 'connected': nothing leads to a first useful result, and nothing measures the path
description: Doc 50 §4 stops after the key check, the model list and the capability probe. No doc designs what the user does with Wilco right after connecting. The user then faces an empty chat with four modes (Ask, Build, Teach, Review; agent-runtime §9) and an autonomy dial. The capability probe makes a real request, but the user never sees it. M6's exit evidence (items 1-8) covers workflows, safety and qualification. It does not count steps, clicks, waits or time from install to a first admitted AI proposal, although D049 item 3 asks for exactly that kind of measurement.
evidence: doc 50 §4 steps 0-9; agent-runtime §9; roadmap m4-v1 M6 exit evidence items 1-8; D049 item 3; no first-run, starter or 'first result' design exists in docs/.
frequency: once: once per setup; this is the moment that decides whether users keep AI on
removal: Eliminate step: the connect-success card offers two or three starter actions computed from the open mission and the bound roles, each with its cost ('$0 on this PC' or 'uses 1 of 50 free requests'), for example 'Explain the selected trigger', 'Name this group', 'Suggest a patrol for the selected squad'. Each is an ordinary workflow that goes through the plan card and admission and produces a real admitted proposal shown as ghosts. A short Drill lesson on Wilco (D028) is the alternative. Measure: add an M6 acceptance test per path (local, free cloud, own key) that counts steps, clicks, confirmations and seconds from a fresh install to the first admitted proposal against a stated budget, using the deterministic fake model.
change_in: doc 50 §4 (a new final step); roadmap m4-v1 M6 exit evidence; architecture testing-strategy; doc 33 (a Wilco Drill lesson)

title: A free setup that meets the proposed UX standard needs three accounts and hand-pasted credentials
description: Doc 52 finds that OpenRouter's one-click preset alone misses the proposed UX standard, even for a light session under the congestion observed. Its recommended free setup is the user's own OpenRouter, Groq and Cloudflare accounts plus a local model. That means three sign-ups, several 18+ age or policy gates, a Cloudflare 'guided token setup' (an API token with the right permission, plus an account id) and a pasted Groq key (D045 item 1). Each step is easy to get wrong. The docs design OAuth only for OpenRouter; the token and key paths have no validation design.
evidence: doc 52 TL;DR, §4 ('What the standard implies'), §6.1 D045 item 1, OQ3; D045 item 1; doc 50 §2.4 (age rules), §4 (other providers), OQ8 (no Cloudflare OAuth known); D050 item 2 (recorded after this row) makes two free providers plus a local model the recommended free setup.
frequency: once: once per setup; the steps where users are most likely to give up
removal: Make wrong input impossible: validate each pasted key or token at once with the provider's own key or token check, which sends no prompt and goes only to the configured provider (within D008). Name the fault in plain words (wrong prefix, missing Workers AI permission, wrong account id) and link straight to the page that fixes it. Fill in endpoints and account ids from the check where the provider returns them. Explain at point of friction: do not ask for three sign-ups up front. Start with one route (local if it fits). Let the quota meter and the stall card show the computed benefit of adding the next one ('Groq would have answered the 7 waits today'), with a one-click add. Resolve together with FR-P-066 and FR-P-032.
change_in: doc 50 §4 (other providers); doc 52 §5.4; D045 Consequences

title: Route lists are heavy to author, and without them congested free hosts raise a stall card on every call
description: Doc 52 proposes user-authored route lists, 'one per role and step kind' (RouteList { role, kind, ... }). With six roles (D024) and five step kinds (D048), that is up to 30 ordered lists. The owner may instead read D023 decision 3 as requiring a click per switch (doc 52 OQ2, RG1). Then, under Confirm and Propose, every busy host raises a stall card after 10 s (UX2). On the free host observed, 1 of 13 attempts was answered in 17.6 minutes, so a session would become a series of cards. A per-run 'resume automatically after the reset' tick adds one more choice to each run.
evidence: doc 52 TL;DR, §5.2 (RouteList, circuit breaker), §5.4 (stall card; plan card tick), §6.2 RG1, OQ2, OQ10; D023 decision 3; D024 item 4.
frequency: session: every session on free cloud
removal: Automate: build the route lists from the connected setups, their qualification per step kind and doc 52 §5.2's fallback order. Show them once, as a single ordered list the user accepts or reorders; per-role and per-kind overrides go under Advanced. Safe default: the stall card's choice carries a 'for this session' option, which records a standing, visible route order. Each later switch is journaled and shown in the run panel and the decision inspector, so D023's 'never silent' holds without a click per call. Route before waiting: skip a host the circuit breaker already knows is cooling, before the user waits on it. D050 (accepted 2026-09-28, after this row was written) item 3 adopts RG1's user-authored route lists, with each move recorded and shown; the 'for this session' stall-card choice is not decided there. Resolve together with FR-M-008, FR-P-067, FR-P-031 and FR-P-066.
change_in: doc 52 §5; D023 decision 3 (owner note); D024 item 4; doc 38 §4.6; a new DG for RG1

title: A plan-card click before runs that cost nothing or almost nothing
description: Doc 40 §6 prices every run that calls a cloud model on the plan card. Under the default Confirm autonomy, the plan card waits for one click per run (doc 38 §5.4). 'Explain a finding' keeps the card because it spends the user's model budget (doc 38 §9). For a local $0 run, or an explanation costing a fraction of a cent, the click adds nothing the turn card could not show. 'Always run without the card' exists only per built-in workflow and per project (doc 38 §5.2), so users must grant it one workflow at a time.
evidence: doc 40 §6 ('Estimate before every run that calls a cloud model'); doc 38 §5.2, §5.4 (Confirm: plan card once per run), §9; D024 item 2.
frequency: constant: every workflow run
removal: Safe default: below a visible, user-changeable threshold (within all caps, tiny cost or free requests, undoable writes only, no deletes or moves), show the estimate inline on the turn card and run on the user's starting gesture, which already carries UserIntent. Never apply this to runs requested by an external agent: they always wait for the editor click (doc 38 §5.2, §9; commands-undo-history §4.4). Never apply it to runs with plugin egress or Preview. Autonomy's safety waits (deletes, moves, Preview, plugin egress) are unchanged (D024 item 3). It needs an owner note on D024 item 2 ('plans are approved once'). Resolve together with FR-P-060 and FR-C-008.
change_in: doc 38 §5.4; doc 40 §6; D024 (owner note)

title: Spending caps have no default values, and the warning about a key with no limit cannot be acted on in the flow
description: D026 and doc 40 §6 define per-run, session and monthly caps per key. Only the per-run cap has a default: the worst case the budget reserves. No doc gives session or monthly defaults, and doc 40 OQ11 leaves caps across several keys open. Doc 50 §4 step 4 warns about a key with no limit, but the OAuth flow cannot set one, so the user must leave for the provider's site. Connecting a paid key with no monthly cap is a surprising default [I], given that the owner treats saving users' API costs as a usability requirement.
evidence: D026 item 2; agent-runtime §12; doc 40 §6 (Caps), OQ11; doc 50 §4 step 4 ('the OAuth flow has no parameter to set one'); roadmap m4-v1 M6 cost UX; no session or monthly cap defaults exist in docs/.
frequency: once: once per key; matters every month
removal: Safe default: when a key that can spend money is connected, the success card pre-fills a visible session cap and monthly cap: a conservative, dated default the user can edit in place. The warning then becomes actionable locally: 'Plotroom will stop at $X a month on this key'. Setups with the free-only guard show '$0: guarded' (doc 50 §4 step 5) instead of a warning.
change_in: D026 (default cap values); doc 40 §6; doc 50 §4 step 4

title: Overloaded words across the setup screens: preset, Ask, profile, tier
description: 'Preset' names several things: the free-model connect presets (D045), harness presets (D048), effort presets (D024), component presets (I34-13), doc 52's 'free-tier Standard', and near it doc 14's prompt profile. Doc 55 OQ1 already counts four uses. 'Ask' is a chat mode (agent-runtime §9), an autonomy level (§11), a workflow step kind (doc 38) and a Dispatch variant (§6). 'Profile' is a target profile (D003), a model profile (doc 51) and a prompt profile (doc 14). 'T0-T4' has four meanings (docs/README §2.2; DG005). A user setting up Wilco can meet 'Ask' twice on one screen, and coding agents and Wilco's own prompts can confuse the meanings.
evidence: doc 55 OQ1; agent-runtime §6, §9, §11; doc 38 §5.4; doc 52 §5.3; docs/README §2.2; DG005; D034 item 3.
frequency: session: every session (user-facing labels); every change set in this area (contributors)
removal: Make wrong input impossible: before the M6 UI lands, a names-table pass (D034 item 3; OWQ-08 (a)) gives each concept one user-facing word. Rename either the chat mode or the autonomy level called 'Ask'. Show harness presets to users as 'tuned for this model'. Drop 'free-tier Standard' (see FR-P-038). Keep internal ids distinct in code (for example separate newtypes for connect presets and harness presets), so the collision cannot reach the type system. Resolve in one names-table pass with FR-P-076, FR-P-052 and FR-P-005.
change_in: D034 names table; doc 55 OQ1; agent-runtime §9, §11; docs/README §2.2; the CODE-INDEX newtype table when the types land

title: Content-policy refusals are discovered mid-run
description: Most free and some paid hosts carry violence wording without a fiction exception (doc 50 §2.3). D045 item 3's disclosure card says only that 'some may refuse it'. D047 item 3's per-item and per-host policy flags are designed for Plotroom's own evaluations (tools/local-qual). Doc 52's router 'skips an entry that fails the privacy or content filters' without saying which user steps count. So a briefing or combat-text step in a user's campaign can be refused by the provider after the call has spent quota. ContentFiltered is recorded as an outcome, but no next action is designed for the user.
evidence: doc 50 §2.3; D045 item 3; D047 item 3 and Consequences (flags proposed for tools/local-qual; a content-filter result is its own outcome, not a wrong answer); doc 52 §5.2 (LimitOutcome::ContentFiltered; route skip rule).
frequency: workflow: per campaign run on hosts with violent-content clauses
removal: Automate: carry D047's two flags into product routing: a per-step 'combat-flavoured' flag on text slots and a per-host policy flag in the dated preset data. The router then sends such steps to local or other route entries before any call is made, and the plan card shows the reason ('briefing text: on this PC (host policy)'). Explain at point of friction: if a refusal still happens, a card names the host and its policy in plain words and offers the next route, template text or a rewrite request. A refusal is never counted as a wrong answer. Extending D047's scope to product routing needs the owner.
change_in: D047 (extend its scope to product routing); doc 52 §5.2; D045 data shape; doc 50 §2.3

title: No designed path when the OS keychain is unavailable
description: Keys live only in the OS keychain, 'never in settings, project files or logs' (doc 50 §4 step 3; crate-map: 'Secrets never in files'). Some machines have no usable keychain: Linux desktops without a running Secret Service, some minimal window managers, portable installs [I]. macOS may ask again for keychain access when an unsigned binary changes. No doc designs what the user sees then. The risk is a failure after the OAuth round trip, or a key that is silently lost.
evidence: doc 50 §4 step 3; crate-map (OS keyring row, plotroom-io::secrets); extensibility (api_key = { keyring = true }); no keychain failure path exists in docs/.
frequency: once: once per setup on affected systems; on macOS possibly after each update [I]
removal: Explain at point of friction, before the OAuth round trip: test keychain access when the connect card opens. If it fails, say why and offer 'Keep this key for this session only (in memory)', clearly labelled; never write it to a file. Add a keyring-failure case with a fake keyring to the connect-flow tests.
change_in: doc 50 §4 step 3; the plotroom-io secrets design (crate-map); architecture testing-strategy

title: External agents poll for a click they cannot see, and get refusals meant for the user
description: workflow.start returns { run, plan }, and the run waits in Planned for a click in the editor (doc 38 §9). The client learns the outcome only by polling workflow.status, because support for MCP's Tasks extension is unknown. When roles are unassigned or a plugin is missing, the start path is 'Plan card; refuse with a fix' (doc 38's guard table), and only the user can apply that fix. The agent loops on status calls, spending tokens on its own provider, and cannot tell the user exactly what to do [I].
evidence: doc 38 §9 (Tools; Approvals stay in the editor; Long runs: 'polling workflow.status works meanwhile'; workflow.list returns 'availability'); doc 38 guard table (Run requested: 'Plan card; refuse with a fix'); doc 38 OQ11 (Tasks support [U]); extensibility §10; agent-runtime §15.
frequency: workflow: every externally started run
removal: Make wrong input impossible: workflow.list already returns 'availability' (doc 38 §9); give that field a typed reason (for example NeedsUserSetup { missing_roles }) rather than adding a new marker, so an agent does not start what cannot run. workflow.start returns a typed AwaitingUserApproval { plan_summary, estimate } state with a sentence the agent can pass on to the user word for word. Eliminate step: workflow.status takes a bounded long-poll, or emits MCP progress notifications where supported, so one call replaces a polling loop. This entry owns the model-side status design. Resolve together with FR-M-007.
change_in: doc 38 §9; extensibility §10; agent-runtime §15

title: The design for turning Wilco on is spread over 15+ files, and the architecture and roadmap predate D045-D048
description: The flow is split across D021-D023, D026, D037, D044-D048, docs 13, 14, 40, 44, 46-53, 55 and 63, and agent-runtime §3, §7, §12 and §13, plus their amendment notes and pointers. The architecture and roadmap (baseline 2026-09-27) have no OpenRouter adapter, OAuth PKCE, aggregator route pinning, keychain connect flow or harness presets. M6's providers are 'Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and OpenAI-compatible local servers'. Doc 50 §4 is an 'implementation placeholder' that needs a DG before code. The choices that gate it are still 'listed, not filed': doc 52 RG1-RG9, the ten in doc 55 §7, and further candidates in docs 50, 51, 56, 57 and 60. (D050 and D051, recorded later the same day, settle part of this: D050 adopts RG1, RG3, RG4 and RG8 and routes RG2, RG5 and RG6 to DG016, DG021, DG019 and DG025.) An M6 implementer must reconcile all of this alone, while AGENTS.md forbids inventing behaviour.
evidence: docs/README §3.4 and §4 rows; roadmap m4-v1 M6 Providers bullet; docs/architecture and docs/roadmap mention D045, D046, D048, OpenRouter and OAuth only for plugin OAuth and a v1.x keyring line; doc 50 §4 status line; doc 52 §6.2; doc 55 §7.
frequency: workflow: every contributor change set in this area
removal: Eliminate step: add one owning architecture section, 'Turning Wilco on', that walks through entry, connect, bind and first result and folds in D045-D048 with their open parts. Add M6 scope rows for the aggregator adapter, OAuth, the keychain connect flow and harness presets. File as DGs the candidates that gate M6: RG9 (dated limit data) and doc 55 §7 item 7 (preset distribution); RG1 (route lists) and RG3 (quota ledger) were decided by D050 after this row was written. Mark the rest deferred, each with a reason.
change_in: architecture agent-runtime (a new section); roadmap m4-v1 M6; docs/design-gap-requests; docs/README §4

title: A separate 'free-tier Standard' effort choice
description: Doc 52 §5.3 suggests that on free tiers the plan card offer Quick or a 'free-tier Standard' (K = 1 on the cloud), and RG5 proposes K = 1 by default on metered and free cloud setups. A second 'Standard' is one more choice, with a subtle difference the user must understand. Yet this is the call reduction the simulation found load-bearing (doc 52 TL;DR).
evidence: doc 52 TL;DR (cloud K = 1 is the reduction that matters), §5.3 ('Effort presets on free tiers'), §5.4 (plan-card mock-up shows 'cloud samples: 1'), §6.2 RG5; DG021; doc 40 R7; D024 item 1.
frequency: constant: every run on free cloud
removal: Safe default: K follows the class of the bound setup automatically: K = 1 on metered and free cloud, the effort table's K on local models. The plan card shows it as 'cloud samples: 1'. No extra preset is needed. Effort stays a budget and never changes the checks (D024 item 1). This is RG5 itself, decided through DG021.
change_in: doc 52 §5.3; RG5 / DG021; doc 40 R7

title: The per-key host allow-list could become one more list to write by hand
description: D046 item 2 adds a per-key allow-list of the hosts behind an aggregator, but what it means waits for DG039. If it starts empty, or lists raw provider slugs, users must learn host names before the free preset works, or the guard blocks every call [I].
evidence: D046 items 2-3; DG039 (open, owner decision on the network boundary); doc 50 §4 steps 1 and 7.
frequency: once: once per key; again when a preset's host changes
removal: Safe default: pre-fill the allow-list from the pinned route of each preset the user accepted on its disclosure card. A new host joins the list only when the user accepts a disclosure card that names it, which keeps D008. Record this as one of DG039's options for the owner.
change_in: D046; DG039; doc 50 §4 step 1

title: Probes and checks spend the user's small free allowance
description: D021's amendment makes the capability probe a real strict-schema request plus a check that reasoning is off, for each setup, and D046 adds periodic re-probes. Doc 50 §4 step 9's 'Check this model' shows '30 of your 50 free requests today'. On OpenRouter's 50-a-day tier these calls compete with the user's own work, and doc 52 finds that even a light session does not complete on that route alone.
evidence: D021 amendment note of 2026-09-27 (the probe tests behaviour); D046 item 2 (periodic re-probes; cadence open, doc 48 OQ11); doc 50 §4 step 9; doc 52 TL;DR, §3.3; D045 item 4 (Plotroom qualifies presets).
frequency: session: every session start and at each re-probe
removal: Eliminate step: Plotroom qualifies every free preset it offers itself (D045 item 4), so user-run checks are offered only for custom endpoints. Safe default: cache probe results per (setup, date) across sessions. Re-probe on a trigger (a catalogue change, a new serving host, a pattern of errors) instead of on a timer, which still catches host and catalogue changes. Show probe calls in the quota meter and the ledger.
change_in: D021 amendment note; D046 item 2 (re-probe cadence, doc 48 OQ11); doc 50 §4 step 9; doc 52 §5.2

title: Editing a harness preset silently lowers what the model is trusted to do
description: Settings, Models, Harness preset offers 'Custom...'. A saved edit is labelled 'custom: unqualified' until 'Check this model on my machine' runs with it (doc 55 §3.5). An unqualified setup gets reduced shapes: Fill only as a confirmed pre-fill, and no Compose or Draft (agent-runtime §7). Nothing designed tells the user this before they save. Doc 55 OQ6 still asks which knobs, samplers included, Settings should expose at all.
evidence: doc 55 §3.5, OQ6; agent-runtime §7; D048 item 6.
frequency: once: rare (advanced users)
removal: Make wrong input impossible: by default, expose only knobs whose effect can be stated in plain language, and keep samplers under Advanced. Before saving, state the computed consequence ('Fill will ask you to confirm each value until checked. Check now: about N min on this PC'), with the check pre-ticked. 'Tuned for this model' is one click away to go back. No grant changes.
change_in: doc 55 §3.5, OQ6; D048 item 6

title: Disclosure cards are long and repeat for each provider
description: D045 item 3 and doc 50 §4 step 1 show a card before any network call with ten kinds of fact: the provider and serving host, limits and reset time, 'as-available', the age rule verbatim, the data route, training and retention, a content note, policy links and 'not legal advice'. Doc 52 §5.4 adds a computed free-tier line. A user connecting the three recommended providers reads three such cards. Long consent screens get skimmed, which defeats their purpose [I].
evidence: D045 item 3; doc 50 §4 step 1; doc 52 §5.4 (disclosure card); doc 52 §4 (three providers recommended).
frequency: once: once per provider
removal: Explain at point of friction: layer the card. Three computed lines come first, for example 'Your mission text goes to OpenRouter, then ModelRun. Not kept, not used for training (as of <date>). Today: 50 requests, about N sessions.' The age rule follows in the first layer, and the rest sits behind 'Details'. The button names the provider. Show the full card again only when one of its facts changes (fits D045 item 5's dating). Nothing is removed from the card, so D045 item 3 holds.
change_in: doc 50 §4 step 1; D045 item 3 (layout only, not what the card says); doc 52 §5.4

title: A pending Wilco proposal either blocks all further editing or is thrown away by the next edit
area: editing: undo/history; commands; Wilco proposals shown as ghosts in the editor
description: Walkthrough: under Confirm autonomy (the default), Wilco proposes a squad as ghosts with a diff card. The user wants to nudge a nearby trigger before accepting. commands-undo-history §4.1 step 4 says a pending preview must be accepted or discarded before any save, export, Preview launch or other command. Doc 38 §7's policy table goes further: any user edit drops pending proposals. Either way the user has to decide before looking around, or loses a proposal that cost tokens and time, and re-running it costs again. Both rules contradict §4.5 of the same architecture file ('the user's own edits never wait for a run; a proposal whose reads changed is re-verified at commit'), and DG011 is still open on what a changed read does. Measure: proposals discarded unseen per session, and tokens spent on discarded proposals.
evidence: commands-undo-history §4.1 step 4, §4.5, §9; core-document-model §11 (Save); doc 38 §7 policy table, row 'User edit: drop pending proposals'; doc 45 §3 ('before save, export, Preview launch or any command'); ui-shell §7; D024 (Confirm is the default); DG011 (open).
frequency: constant: every Wilco turn under the default autonomy
removal: Eliminate the step. Pending proposals stay pending while the user edits, and read-set freshness re-verifies them when accepted (DG011 option C). Only save, export and Preview require resolution, and there the safe default is 'continue without it, keep it pending'. The saved bytes are still the pre-proposal bytes, so the existing dirty-state test holds. A proposal whose reads changed gets a Stale badge and a 're-plan' button instead of vanishing.
change_in: commands-undo-history §4.1, §4.5; doc 38 §7 (fold); core-document-model §11; DG011; testing-strategy dirty-state test
effort: S design fold; M implementation (the freshness check already exists)

title: Script fields in the classic dialogs are checked only when OK is pressed
area: editing: faithful editor modes; unit/trigger/waypoint dialogs; Teller
description: Walkthrough: open a trigger, type a condition with a typo or a boolean '==', press OK. The DialogSession runs admission, including the engine-parity check_field (CanDestroy), only at OK. So the first error appears after the user thinks they are done. That is the late-error pattern doc 09 P2 names as the original editor's worst pain ('script fields are blind'). Teller's completion, hover and mission-name index are designed for the Script editor panel. Nothing says the dialogs' condition, On Activation and init fields use them, so users type unit and marker names from memory. Measure: OK presses that return a rejection, per session.
evidence: commands-undo-history §10 (OK builds a batch and runs admission hosting the CanDestroy parity checks); ui-shell §4 (dialogs) and §6 (Teller features listed only for the Script editor panel); validation-and-lints §9 (check_field: first error with caret offset); doc 09 P2, P7; roadmap M2 goal ('integrated field checking'); doc 37 §7 specifies live checks only for raw mode.
frequency: constant: every trigger, waypoint and init edit
removal: Automate, and make wrong input impossible. Every script-bearing dialog field uses the same Teller-backed text widget as the script editor. It runs check_field in the field's mode on each change against the dialog's Scratch (Teller calls are in the <0.1 s class, doc 61), shows the caret-positioned error inline, and completes mission names, markers and the commands available on the profile. OK stays the only commit and admission still re-checks, so parity is unchanged.
change_in: ui-shell §4; commands-undo-history §10 (DialogSession); plotroom-view, plotroom-teller, plotroom-ui-classic; roadmap M2 exit evidence

title: A gesture the core refuses has no designed feedback, so nothing seems to happen
area: editing: placing units, groups, waypoints, triggers; admission
description: Walkthroughs: double-click to insert a unit within 100 m of a group that already has 12 units (auto-join); drag a radio trigger onto a slot a module's allocator owns; drag-link something that would leave a dangling reference. Admission returns a typed Rejection, which 'never enters history' (§4.1 step 3), and failure class 1 refuses the whole group (§5). ui-shell only designs surfaces for findings on committed content (Problems panel, squiggles, map glyphs). Where a refused gesture is shown is not specified, which risks a silent failure. The original editor showed these late, as modal boxes, or not at all (doc 09 P7).
evidence: commands-undo-history §4.1 step 3, §5 failure class 1; ui-shell §3 (insert, 100 m auto-join), §6 (Problems); validation-and-lints §13 (editor surfaces); doc 31 §4.5 (radio allocator); doc 09 P7; roadmap M2 ('live engine-limit checks').
