title: A busy free host gets retried on the same endpoint, then raises a stall card on every decision
area: model-facing: provider errors and rate limits
description: Walk-through: a free-tier Pick receives an upstream 429 with retry_after 0.12-0.77 s. Doc 48's retry rule and doc 51 §4.6 retry 408/429/5xx on the same endpoint and honour Retry-After. Doc 38 §4.6 and D023 decision 3 forbid moving the call to another setup without a click. The harness therefore spends its retry budget on a host that stays throttled for 15 minutes or more. Under Confirm autonomy it then shows the stall card again for every decision, and the user makes the same choice dozens of times. Two overlapping taxonomies describe the same outcomes: doc 51's ProviderFailure::RateLimited{scope} and doc 52's LimitOutcome, so an adapter author has to choose one (doc 51 §4.7 already charges upstream RateLimited to endpoint dependability, not to model accuracy).
evidence: doc 52 TL;DR and §2.3 (1 of 13 attempts answered in 17.6 min; retry_after 0.12-0.77 s while the throttle lasted more than 15 min), §3.3 (OpenRouter :free alone answers 34-42% of a light session's decisions; no simulated day completes), §5.1 principle 1, §6.1 (conflict between D023 decision 3 and doc 38 §4.6), §6.2 (RG1 and RG2, not filed when swept; D050 adopts RG1 and routes RG2 to DG016); doc 51 §4.6-§4.7 (ProviderFailure) and doc 52 §5.2 (LimitOutcome) overlap; doc 48 §7 retry rule (408/429/5xx with Retry-After).
frequency: constant: every decision on congested free cloud tiers; any paid host under load
removal: Automate, as the user's standing choice. Keep one LimitOutcome taxonomy in plotroom-provider. An upstream 429 cools that host and reroutes the call at once along a user-authored route list (RG1), and every switch is recorded in the run panel and the inspector, which keeps the glass box. Only account-scoped 429s follow Retry-After. Interactive calls get at most 2 retries per endpoint (UX9). The stall card appears only when the list is exhausted. D050 (accepted 2026-09-28, after this row was written) adopts this reading of D023 decision 3 in items 1, 3 and 4: route lists the user wrote or accepted, a move on a limit outcome without a click per move, each move recorded and shown, and at most 2 immediate retries per endpoint; merging doc 51's ProviderFailure into LimitOutcome is still open. tools/quota-sim already models the strategies. Resolve together with FR-P-032 and FR-P-067.
change_in: D023 decision 3 (owner reading); D021; doc 51 §4.6-§4.7; doc 38 §4.6; doc 48 retry rule; file RG1 and RG2 as DGs; plotroom-provider, plotroom-provider-http
effort: M (an owner decision plus one enum and the router)

title: IntentFill and the Selector run before any work on every free-text Wilco message
description: Walk-through: the user types 'put a BMP patrol around the village north of the airfield'. Free text always goes IntentFill then Dispatch. On a 3-4B setup, IntentFill is either per-field Picks (task, side, size, posture, era, plus a place span) or a whole-record pre-fill the user must confirm, because unqualified setups run freedom level FR2. A Selector Pick follows, and only then do the workflow's own steps begin. That is 2-7 model calls and possibly one click before any real work. Menus, context actions and the palette already skip extraction (doc 21 §4.2, 'rung 0'), /commands are parsed with no model call (agent-runtime §9), and DP-02's fallback is the code RuleSelector (D023 item 5); the gap is free text, where code does not first fill fields from the UI context and aliases, although the selection, the open panel and the map cursor often already fix the workflow and several of the fields.
evidence: agent-runtime §6 ('Clarification is computed') and §9; doc 21 §4.2; doc 53 §1.2 (DP-01 is 12 of 35 decisions in a 30-minute session; DP-02 is at most 1 per free-text request; DP-13); doc 63 §4.2 (intent fill in one call only at 26-30B MoE or cloud), §4.1 (unqualified setups run freedom level FR2); doc 58 A2 (alias rules, then one Pick per field); doc 52 §5.3 (50% of intent Fills skippable by gestures [U]); doc 56 DS1 (the need to ask is computed); D023 item 5.
frequency: constant: every free-text chat message
removal: Eliminate the step. Code-first intake: lexicon and alias rules, catalog and place-name matches and the UI context (selection, open panel, cursor) fill every field they can, with quotes computed by code (see FR-M-020). Only the fields that remain open go to the model. The Selector runs only when more than one compatible workflow remains. /commands, context menus and palette starts keep skipping intake entirely.
change_in: agent-runtime §6, §9; doc 21 §4.1; doc 53 DP-01/DP-02; plotroom-decide, plotroom-wilco

title: One unit choice can take up to four sequential faceted Picks
description: Walk-through: 'add a squad' runs side, kind, role group, role: one capsule and one interactive L1 wait per facet. This happens even when the request, IntentFill, the target group's side or the mod set already fixes a facet, and when a facet has only one option left after hard filters. DG006's bench has not run, so nothing yet shows that facets save more than they cost. agent-runtime §6 already says 'When code knows the deciding fact, it filters the menu instead of asking'; this extends that to skipping facets.
evidence: agent-runtime §6 (catalog menus are faceted; doc 42 §2.4; I42-25), §16 item 2; DG006 (open; bench E4); doc 56 DS6 (a two-level router must beat a flat menu at the same information budget); doc 60 §2.7 and P-08 (back off at the last confident facet); doc 53 §1.1 (L1 target <= 1-2 s per Pick).
frequency: constant: every catalog Pick (unit, vehicle, squad)
removal: Eliminate the step. Code skips any facet that admitted intent fields or hard filters (profile, mod set, the group's side) already decide, or that has at most one option. Adjacent facets are merged into one flat Pick when their options fit MENU_MAX. The chain stops at the last confident facet and shows the children as a top-k card. Merging and stopping rules are decided with DG006's bench E4.
change_in: agent-runtime §6; DG006; doc 25 §6.2; doc 42 §2.4; plotroom-decide

title: Repair shows one finding per turn, so answers with several findings run out of budget
description: Walk-through: a 4B model writes a trigger condition that uses sleep, isNil and == on Booleans, which gives three independent parity findings. Repair quotes one finding per turn, and R is 1/2/3 by effort. At Quick (R = 1) one finding is repaired, then on_fail keeps the default. The model never sees the other two findings, and the user loses the step. At higher effort the three findings cost three sequential round trips. External evidence says admissible alternatives carry most of the gain, that grouping related errors was decisive in one ablation, and that nearly all gains come in 1-3 rounds.
evidence: agent-runtime §6 ('Repair quotes one finding per turn'); doc 61 §3 (R = 1/2/3 by effort), §2.2-§2.3, §4.6 steps 4-7; doc 62 §6.9 tension (RustAssistant ablation; one root per turn with same-field findings grouped) and §10 item 8; doc 25 §7.2; doc 23 §13.4 (model-shaped diagnostic schema).
frequency: workflow: every script or text repair
removal: Eliminate steps. Each turn repairs one root finding, and every introduced finding on the same field or entity is grouped into one card (cap about 3 findings and 200 tokens, to be measured). On resample paths, all introduced findings are stated as facts (doc 61 §4.6 step 6). Keep TG9's 'no progress' stop. Checks and stops are unchanged.
change_in: agent-runtime §6; doc 25 §7.2; doc 61 §4.6; validation-and-lints §9 (model-shaped diagnostics); plotroom-decide

title: Format failures are resent unchanged on deterministic setups, wasting the strike budget
area: model-facing: repair loops and invalid answers
description: Walk-through: a setup with greedy or temperature-0 decoding (doc 55 H-R1, Granite's recipe), or an endpoint that ignores the seed, returns a wrapper tag or an empty answer (InvalidAnswer). Doc 51 §4.6 then resamples 'with a new seed'. Under such decoding the same capsule gives the same reply, so each retry is wasted until the three-strike stop, and the inspector reports the failure as flaky when it is systematic. Under sampled decoding a new seed does change the reply, and Pick resamples already change bytes because menus are re-permuted per sample; the waste is specific to deterministic setups. Doc 56 VR1 instead appends one fixed replacement message, so the two designs disagree.
evidence: doc 51 §4.6 (resample with a new seed; three strikes), §4.7 (Empty{deterministic}); D022 amendment (every sampler value is pinned, including the seed); doc 55 §6.3 (Granite greedy decoding with one-pass scoring), H-R1; doc 60 §2.14 (under greedy scoring, identical-prompt pass^k equals accuracy); doc 56 VR1; doc 51 TL;DR (wrapper-tag JSON drops Phi-4 to 1.5-11.0); agent-runtime §6 (menus re-permuted per sample).
frequency: workflow: per format failure; frequent on unprobed or weak setups
removal: Eliminate the step. Never resend a byte-identical capsule on a deterministic setup: a retry must change code-owned bytes (VR1's fixed format reminder appended at the tail, the next menu permutation, or the profile's stricter schema mode), or go straight to on_fail and record the format failure as a 'known rough edge' of the preset (doc 60 P-14). Only retry mechanics change.
change_in: doc 51 §4.6; doc 56 VR1; DG016 (retry accounting); plotroom-decide

title: Every Pick and Fill must start with a 'why' field that was never measured
area: model-facing: answer schema and token waste
description: Walk-through: every Pick and Fill schema puts a bounded 'why' (25-40 words, 40-160 characters) before the answer. On a 4B local model, Pick decode already takes 106-430 ms. The 'why' adds up to about 40 decode tokens per call, multiplied by K samples, for every decision. The runs that produced today's qualification evidence contained 0 'why' records, so the doctrinal default is not the configuration that was measured. The literature says prompted reasoning at 4-8B lowers classification accuracy and reasoning lowers abstention. Hypothesis H5 is untested.
evidence: doc 25 §2.4, §4.3-§4.4, H5; doc 38 §3.2 'model' row ('Pick and Fill lead with a bounded why'); doc 21 §3; doc 59 TL;DR, §3.1 (0 why records in the re-counted set), SR7, §7 item 6; doc 53 §3 (decode times), R7, T10 (tension with doc 25 §4.3); doc 60 §2.11 and P-13.
frequency: constant: every Pick and Fill call
removal: Safe default. No 'why' field by default. It becomes a D048 preset knob per (model, DecisionKind), switched on only where doc 53 R7 or doc 59 A10 shows a gain (doc 59 suggests keeping a bounded 'why' on escape-bearing kinds, which the knob allows). The inspector's 'why' is built by code from the recorded sub-answers (doc 60 P-13), which keeps D010 and matches agent-runtime §9.
change_in: doc 25 §2.4, §4.3-§4.4; doc 38 §3.2-§3.3; agent-runtime §6; doc 55 knob catalogue

title: The first call to an unprobed endpoint can fail on request shape
area: model-facing: model quirks and provider setup
description: Walk-through: the user connects a model or endpoint that model-profiles.csv does not cover. The owner rule pins every sampler value, but endpoints reject parameters. Current Claude models reject temperature. Qwen3.8 returns HTTP 500 on reasoning 'high'. Gemini Flash rejects 'minimal'. Moonshot rejects its toggle together with an effort level. OpenRouter with require_parameters=true turns an unsupported pinned key into a 404 'no endpoint'. Profile fields start as Unprobed, 'a setup is executable only when every field its step kind needs is present', and re-check probes are opt-in. The first Pick therefore fails with an InvalidRequest or StructuralRequest the user cannot interpret, or the setup is refused.
evidence: agent-runtime §3 and the D022 amendment (every request pins every sampler value); doc 40 R7 (Claude rejects temperature); doc 51 TL;DR (Qwen3.8 HTTP 500 on high; Gemini rejects minimal; knob conflicts), §4.2 (Z2 executability), §4.3 (sampler_accepted facts), §4.8 (re-checks opt-in, off by default); doc 52 §5.2 (NoEndpointForPolicy).
frequency: once: once per new setup or endpoint; blocks when it happens
removal: Safe default, then automate. A strict 'unknown endpoint' profile omits every sampler key not proven accepted, turns thinking off in the most common encoding with a FloorAt fallback, uses JsonObjectPlusPrompt schema mode and sets no cache, so the first call works. Every omitted sampler key is recorded in the run record as 'server default, unknown', so results stay attributable, and the setup stays unqualified until the canary has filled the fields, which keeps D022's comparability aim. A connect-time canary (a few tiny synthetic requests, user-started, with its call count and cost shown on the connect card before it runs) fills the tri-state fields. Each 400/404/500 body is mapped to the field that caused it, recorded as No{run_id} and retried once. The D022 amendment wording ('pins every accepted key') is an owner decision.
change_in: doc 51 §4.2-§4.3, §4.8; D022 amendment wording (owner); agent-runtime §3; plotroom-provider-http

title: Free tiers capped by tokens run out quickly on capsules sized for paid caches
area: model-facing: capsule size and rate limits
description: Walk-through: on Groq's 8K tokens a minute or Cloudflare's neuron budget, every Pick carries the full frozen stage prefix: doctrine, design-sensibility core and lens, primer sections, cards, exemplars and schema text, about 1,230 tokens, plus the request, digest and menu. The layout is designed to clear paid providers' cache minimums (BP1 needs about 1,024 tokens on Sonnet 5), but token-metered free tiers that do not cache pay for every token, and only a few Picks fit per minute. No lean profile exists yet (RG6 is not filed).
evidence: doc 52 TL;DR ('Capsule size decides whether token-capped tiers ... are usable at all'), §1.4 and §5.3 (a campaign day on one Groq model goes from 9% to 94% with lean capsules), RG6; doc 40 §1.1 (1,230-token stage prefix), §4.1 (BP1 minimum), R11; doc 57 §4.1 C8 (cache semantics per provider as data); DG019, DG025.
frequency: constant: every call on token-capped free tiers
removal: Safe default. The capsule profile is chosen from the endpoint profile's cache and meter facts. Where cached tokens are neither cached nor free, a lean profile applies: code-signalled primer sections and cards only, no taste core or lens on Picks that do not use taste, no exemplars. It is qualified as a preset knob (D048), so it stays inside the qualification regime. Text is never added to reach a cache minimum on an endpoint that does not cache.
change_in: doc 40 §4.1, R11; doc 55 knobs; file RG6; DG019, DG025; plotroom-decide

title: Cards that depend on the decision sit in the frozen cache prefix
description: Walk-through: the capsule's frozen stage prefix holds 'code-picked primer sections and cards' above BP1. Cards are chosen by four signals, and two of them change with every decision: the tokens of the text under repair and the codes of the current diagnostics. Either the frozen prefix changes per decision, which misses the cache, breaks the one-namespace-per-(stage, DecisionKind) rule, breaks 'Nothing volatile sits above a breakpoint' and fails the golden prefix test, or cards are chosen only from the stable signals and the repair-relevant cards are missing. In local-qual the cards sat in the user message and were re-processed on every call. Card effects also change sign by model.
evidence: agent-runtime §6 (capsule segment 1; 'Nothing volatile sits above a breakpoint'), §8 (four signals); doc 30 §4.2; doc 40 §4.1 (cards above BP1), R2-R4; doc 57 §4.2 (pick-hard with cards: 13% cached, the ~140-token card re-processed every call), §5.1 CL1; doc 55 §1.1 (the same card helps Qwen on HK01 and hurts it on HM04 and HW03).
frequency: constant: every capsule that carries cards
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Use two card slots with type-level volatility tiers (doc 57 CL1), so a wrong placement is a type error. Stage cards (chosen by field kind and step) go above BP1. Decision cards (chosen by repair tokens and diagnostics) go in the tail after the digest. The renderer refuses a decision-tier card in the stage section, a golden prefix test covers it, and card policy per model stays a preset knob.
change_in: agent-runtime §6, §8; doc 40 §4.1; doc 30 §4.2; doc 57 CL1; plotroom-decide

title: The primer tells every model to call lookup tools that most steps do not offer
area: model-facing: tool schemas and model-facing text
description: Walk-through: Wilco loads mission-primer before mission work. Its 'How to work' section says to look facts up with catalog.find, island.places, script.command, reference.search and reference.card, to check every script with script.check, and to call next_step(). It adds 'Tool names are provisional; yours win'. Pick and Fill capsules expose no tools, and TS1 (every unqualified setup, which today means every setup) has no pull tools. A weak model told to call a tool it does not have either writes call-shaped text into its JSON answer (InvalidAnswer) or wastes a turn. In chat modes, tools that are visible but not allowed in the current step come back as ToolNotInStep, another wasted round trip. External agents get the same primer while their manifest uses different names.
evidence: skills/mission-primer/SKILL.md §1 items 1, 3 and 5; agent-runtime §8 ('Weak models never fetch knowledge'; anchor-addressed primer sections), §2 (ToolNotInStep); doc 61 §4.10 (TS1: no pull tools); doc 40 §4.1 (no tools for Pick and Fill); DG023 option B; doc 38 §9 (the primer is served to external agents); doc 57 §5.1 CL7 (lint: no tool named that the step does not offer); D019 (safe profile).
frequency: constant: every capsule carrying primer §1; every MCP session
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Render the primer's 'How to work' section per surface level and per client from the actual callable set, using the primer's anchor-addressed sections. At TS1 it says 'facts are given to you in cards; answer from the menu'. At TS2+ and over MCP it names the real tools. Remove the 'yours win' hedge. The static SKILL.md stays valid under D019's safe profile. CL7 and PK2 lints fail CI on any tool name outside the step's set. In chat, local grammars mask out-of-step tools. Resolve together with FR-M-018.
change_in: skills/mission-primer/SKILL.md; doc 30 §5.2; agent-runtime §8; DG023; doc 57 CL7; testing-strategy §14

title: The same tools go by different names across prompts, digests and error text
description: Walk-through: a model reads a Session Digest line 'Lookup handles: journal.find, mission.get, catalog.search' and calls catalog.search, but the primer and doc 30 name catalog.find, and doc 61 names mission.find, not mission.get. Error text says 'call list_commands for valid ids', but no manifest lists list_commands. The primer's next_step() has no row in DG032's family, and validate_script, check_field and script.check coexist. Two knowledge tool families have the same job: doc 33's list_concepts, explain_concept and explain_instance, and doc 30's reference.search and reference.card for the same Standing Orders store, so a weak model with both in its tool set must choose between near-synonyms. A small model trusts every name it is shown, so each mismatch becomes an unknown-tool refusal and a wasted turn. DG032 is still open, so every name is provisional, and any wording measured now changes the qualification key later. Merged from a duplicate wilco-ux finding about the two knowledge tool families.
evidence: doc 57 §3.6 (digest 'Lookup' line); doc 12 §5 (catalog.search); doc 30 §4.4, open question 7, and the primer (catalog.find, next_step()); doc 33 §6.1 ('Two tool families with the same job make a small model pick between near-synonyms, so one family should survive'); doc 61 §4.3 (mission.find); commands-undo-history §3 (list_commands); agent-runtime §8 (names provisional until DG032); DG032 (open; option C retires list_concepts, explain_concept and bare explain_instance); doc 56 PK2; doc 60 P-02 (wording hash in the qualification key).
frequency: constant: every model-facing text that names a tool; every explain or teach call
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Decide DG032 (one family, one name per job, explain_instance included; aliases only on the MCP server, if at all), then generate every model-facing name (capsules, digest templates, primer, error text, the MCP manifest) from the one registry. The PK2 and CL7 CI gates fail on unknown names, and they apply before any model-facing wording is frozen or measured. Add a registry test that no two tools in one step's tool set share a job tag. Resolve together with FR-M-004, FR-M-017 and FR-M-021.
change_in: DG032; doc 57 §3.6; commands-undo-history §3; skills/mission-primer; doc 12 §5; doc 30 §4.4; doc 33 §6.1; agent-runtime §8; testing-strategy §14

title: Letter-coded Fill fields share one alphabet, so a letter meant for another field passes silently
description: Walk-through: under DG024's recommended option B, cloud Fill fields whose values come from computed sets become letter fields over menus printed in the capsule, and admission checks membership. A Fill with two such fields (for example waypoint type and behaviour, or roll scope and trigger timing) prints two A-G menus. A model that answers field 2 with the letter it read in field 1's menu produces a valid letter, membership passes, and the wrong value is admitted silently. Doc 56 DS2 requires visibly distinct lists and a separate 'wrong list' failure type, and shared letters make that failure impossible to detect.
evidence: DG024 option B and its recommended resolution; doc 56 DS2 ('Two closed value lists share a step only if visibly distinct, and a wrong-list value is its own failure type'); doc 55 §1.1 (Gemma HV01 PerCampaign vs PerTurn, 7 of 24); agent-runtime §6 (strict admission).
frequency: constant: every cloud Fill with two or more computed-set fields
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Use disjoint label sets per field within one request (A-G for the first field, P-V for the second, or field-prefixed codes), so a label from the wrong field fails membership as a typed wrong-list finding. Disjoint labels fit a frozen per-DecisionKind schema, so caching is kept. On small setups, prefer per-field Picks (doc 53 DP-12). Write this into DG024 before it is decided, and design it with the cloud Pick enum (FR-M-025).
change_in: DG024; doc 30 §4.2; doc 25 §4.3; doc 56 DS2; plotroom-decide

title: The model must copy request quotes exactly, and paraphrases are refused
description: Walk-through: IntentFill fields are quoted spans, and admission requires each quote to be a substring of the request. The model has to reproduce spans character for character. Qwen3.5-4B paraphrased spans and mixed languages in Fill. Granite 4.1 3B left named places empty. Requests in Czech, Polish or Russian with diacritics are more fragile still. Each paraphrase is a refused quote, which costs a repair turn or drops the field to a question card.
evidence: agent-runtime §6 ('IntentFill quotes must be substrings of the request'); doc 21 §4.1; doc 55 TL;DR and §1.1 (Qwen paraphrase and language mixing; Granite 6 of 6 empty places), H-R3 (verbatim span grammar); doc 56 DS2 (spans picked by index; code copies); doc 60 §2.9 (code proposes, the model selects, code copies).
frequency: constant: about 12 of 35 decisions per session (DP-01)
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Code proposes candidate spans (island place names, catalog aliases, n-grams around cue words) and the model picks an index, then code copies the characters, so admission is unchanged. Where a span must stay the model's own choice, a local verbatim-span grammar restricts it to substrings of the request; on cloud endpoints without grammars, the substring check stays as the fallback. Resolve together with FR-M-009.
change_in: agent-runtime §6; doc 21 §4.1; doc 53 DP-01; plotroom-decide

title: Tool manifests are built from contributor doc comments, one tool per command
area: model-facing: tool schemas and cache stability
description: Walk-through: an external agent connects and receives one tool per AgentCallable command. Each description is the Rust /// comment that AGENTS.md requires to explain what, why and invariants for maintainers, including Rust identifiers and DG references. Every request carries all these schemas. Doc 40's defer_loading covers plugin tools only, and no size strategy is stated for MCP. For Wilco, any doc-comment edit changes the manifest bytes, which breaks the cache and alters qualified wording, and the text is written for the wrong reader.
evidence: commands-undo-history §3 ('Tool schemas and descriptions come from /// docs via schemars'; MCP tools generated from the registry); AGENTS.md comment rules; doc 62 §6.8; doc 40 R5 (defer_loading past about 10 tools or 10K tokens, plugins only); extensibility §10; doc 11 (8-12 tools as the default set); doc 60 P-02 (wording hash).
frequency: constant: every Wilco chat request with tools; every MCP request
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Model-facing descriptions come only from the knowledge store, keyed by CommandId (cards of at most 150 words in product vocabulary), or from explicit #[schemars(description)]. A CI check rejects Rust identifiers and host paths, and a manifest golden test pins the bytes. MCP exposes a small fixed set (mission query, command.describe, changeset.propose, workflow.*) and serves per-command schemas as resources on demand; this changes extensibility §10's 'generated from the command registry' and depends on the batch-proposal tool of FR-M-007. Every call is still admitted by the runtime, so scope is unchanged. Resolve together with FR-M-018.
change_in: commands-undo-history §3; doc 62 §6.8 (fold); extensibility §10; doc 40 R5; plotroom-mcp, plotroom-wilco

title: Samples and repairs on the default local models re-read the whole request and digest
description: Walk-through: the default local models are hybrid (Qwen3.5-4B) or sliding-window (Gemma 4), and llama-server on them reuses a cached prefix only at message boundaries. Today's capsule puts the request, digest, cards and permuted menu in one user message. Every extra sample, repair or EXPLAIN therefore re-processes about 900 tokens, which takes 2.7-4.2 s each, so a K = 3 Pick loses 5-8 s on steps meant to answer in 1-2 s. Doc 51 V10 builds each repair as a fresh single-turn capsule, while doc 57 TE-G3 appends repairs at the tail. The two are unresolved.
evidence: doc 57 TL;DR and §4.2 (pick-hard reused only the 58-token system message on 449 of 452 calls, 20% cached; Fill prefill fell from 1.6-2.3 s cold to 0.1-0.4 s warm), §4.3 (split layout), CL2, CL4, CL5, TE-G1, TE-G3, §6.3 (V10 conflict); doc 51 §4.6 (fresh repair capsule); doc 53 §1.1 (L1 target).
frequency: constant: every multi-sample decision and every repair on local setups
removal: Automate. Adopt the split layout (system = stage pack; user 1 = request and digest; a fixed acknowledgement; user 2 = sample tail) as a preset field, decided per model family by experiment E13, so it is measured before adoption. Auxiliary calls append to the decision's exact capsule bytes (CL4), and golden prefix tests run through the chat template (CL2). Resolve V10 against TE-G3 in one DG.
change_in: doc 40 §4.1; doc 51 §4.6 (V10); doc 57 TE-G1, TE-G3; doc 55 preset fields; plotroom-decide, plotroom-provider-http
effort: M (layout, tests and one E13 run)

title: Escape answers compete with real options, and Fill has no way to say 'not stated'
description: Walk-through: every menu ends with X none_fit and Q ask, but they sit in the same distribution as the real options. Qwen3.5-4B missed the near-fit escape HM04 in 12 of 24 samples. Reasoning training lowers abstention by 24% on average. Without an explicit escape, an outside classifier flagged 0 of 30 out-of-scope items at 0.99, and it chose a 'don't know' option in 72 of 72 calls when that option was offered. Fill has no channel for 'the request does not say': Granite left places empty in 6 of 6 samples, and the size field was right only 14-19 of 24 times, so models invent values instead of abstaining. A missed X admits a near-fit option silently, and a wrong Q costs the user a card.
evidence: doc 55 TL;DR (HM04 12 of 24), H-Q2; doc 59 TL;DR [21], §3.2, S7 (coverage check); doc 60 §2.4 (existence gate, P-04), §2.9 ('stated?' gate, P-05); doc 56 EQ4, DS1; agent-runtime §6 (escapes).
frequency: constant: every near-fit Pick; every Fill with optional or judgement fields
removal: Automate, so code decides the escape. An independent existence gate and a per-field 'stated?' gate are read in the same pass, and code-side coverage checks run beside them. Code maps the results to X, to Q, or to 'not stated', which becomes a visible default chip or a question card, which improves the glass box. X and Q stay as menu letters, and confidence never admits an answer. This is a research proposal that needs calibration on the tuning split.
change_in: agent-runtime §6; doc 25 §6.2; doc 21 §3.2; doc 53 §4; doc 55 H-Q2; plotroom-decide
effort: M (gates plus calibration on the tuning split)

title: Budget units disagree, and a slot's context window can be smaller than the one assumed
area: model-facing: capsule budgets and context windows
description: Walk-through: a capsule is counted against an '8K' window but reaches a llama-server slot whose served context depends on -c, the slot count and KV sharing; local-qual ran 4 slots on an 8,192-token context. The server refuses an over-long prompt ('exceeds the available context size'), or the harness shrinks the digest by relevance, so the model decides with less context than its qualification assumed. The docs budget in incompatible units: doc 57 TE-G7 uses window fractions, doc 56's rejected-designs list includes 'budgets as a fraction of a window', doc 12 §5.3 uses an absolute 1.5K and doc 38 §3.5 uses 2%. The sidecar start-up line sets -c without a slot count.
evidence: doc 57 §3.2 (rules 1-3), §4.2 (4 slots on 8,192; over-long prompts rejected), LO1-LO3 (read n_ctx per slot; an unknown window fails closed), TE-G7; agent-runtime §3 (sidecar -c <ctx>); doc 56 §9 tension 1 and §10 item 7; doc 12 §5.3; doc 38 §3.5; doc 40 §1.1 (1,230-token prefix).
frequency: workflow: every local capsule near the window; every step definition
removal: Automate. Use one budget unit: tokens derived from the per-slot n_ctx read back at connect, with the output and thinking reserve subtracted first. The sidecar sets -c = slots x (largest qualified capsule + reserve). The definition compiler rejects a step whose fixed part cannot fit the smallest qualified per-slot window. One DG reconciles docs 12, 38, 56 and 57.
change_in: agent-runtime §3; doc 57 TE-G7; doc 56 WR6 and §10 item 7; doc 12 §5.3; doc 38 §3.5; plotroom-model-manager, plotroom-workflow

title: A small prompt-pack edit drops every qualified setup back to the smallest steps
description: Walk-through: a release rewords one card sentence for waypoint menus. If qualification is keyed by pack version or by a wording hash over the whole pack, every DecisionKind's badges become void. The user's setup falls to freedom level FR2 and TS1 on every kind until a re-check that costs them quota or GPU time, and each wording tweak forces contributors to re-run 14+ trials per kind and model. DG012 recommends semver rules, while doc 60 P-02 and doc 56 MA6 treat any wording change as a new configuration, so the docs pull in different directions.
evidence: DG012 (options A-C; the recommended C keeps the 'smallest safe shape' until re-checked); doc 60 §2.2 and P-02; doc 56 MA6; D048 item 5; doc 63 §4.4 (the wording hash joins the key), §4.6 (levels only go down mid-run).
frequency: once: every release that touches model-facing text
removal: Automate. Key wording hashes per DecisionKind, over the exact prompt bytes that kind renders, so only kinds whose bytes changed are voided; this is more precise than semver and cannot be mislabelled, and a change to the shared prefix still voids every kind, which is correct. The release pipeline re-runs must-pass cases and a quick batch for the changed kinds and ships refreshed records for shipped presets. A user-run record rebinds automatically when its kind's bytes are unchanged. The UI says 'requalifying: kinds X, Y' instead of dropping every level at once. Resolve together with FR-P-064.
change_in: DG012; doc 60 P-02; doc 56 MA6; doc 63 §4.4; plotroom-evals, plotroom-provider

title: Connecting an MCP client means manual setup, and a per-session token would break it every launch
description: Walk-through: the user enables the MCP server, then has to find the port and token and hand-write the client's configuration. Doc 15 proposes 'a per-session token'. If the token or a random port changes at each editor launch, the external agent's first call of the day fails authentication, and the agent cannot fix that itself. The token's lifetime, the port and the client configuration are not specified anywhere.
evidence: doc 15 §11 item 10 ('require a per-session token'); extensibility §10 (loopback, token-authenticated; no lifecycle); agent-runtime §15; crate-map plotroom-mcp row; doc 50 §4 step 3 (keys in the OS keychain); doc 56 PK3 (exact Host check against DNS rebinding); roadmap M4.
frequency: once: once per client setup; per launch if tokens are per session
removal: Automate. Store a stable per-install token in the OS keychain (as doc 50 §4 step 3 does for keys), not in plain app-data settings; show it only on an explicit copy, and offer rotate and revoke. Use a stable default port with a recorded fallback, and keep the loopback bind and the exact Host check (doc 56 PK3). A 'Copy connection config' action puts ready snippets for common MCP clients on the clipboard only; the user pastes them, and Plotroom writes no other application's files. Authentication errors state the fix in words, for example 'token rotated in Settings, External agents; copy the new config'. Copying the config adds no capability (the outbound-exposure rule). Resolve together with FR-P-020.
change_in: extensibility §10; agent-runtime §15; ui-shell (Settings); plotroom-mcp

title: The cloud Pick schema allows letters A-Z although menus never exceed 7 options
description: Walk-through: the frozen cloud Pick schema allows 'letters A-Z plus the X and Q escapes', but MENU_MAX is 7. X and Q are inside A-Z, so a cloud model can emit any of 17 letters that no menu ever uses. Each one is admitted by the schema, refused at membership and repaired in an extra turn. Locally the grammar already allows exactly the menu's letters.
evidence: doc 40 §4.1 (format line), R5; agent-runtime §6 (MENU_MAX = 7, a DG006 option C proposal); DG024 option B ('Cloud models can emit an invalid letter (refused, then repaired)'); doc 25 §4.4 (local grammar 'exactly A|B|C|X').
frequency: constant: exposure on every cloud Pick; occasional wasted repair
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Generate the frozen cloud enum from MENU_MAX (A-G, X, Q). It stays one schema per DecisionKind, so caching is unchanged; a later DG006 change to MENU_MAX alters every schema, and with it the cache and qualification keys, which is acceptable. Membership checks still catch letters beyond the current menu's size. Design the enum together with the disjoint Fill labels of FR-M-019.
change_in: doc 40 §4.1; DG015; DG024; DG006; plotroom-decide

title: The default local grammar lets Gemma pad JSON answers with whitespace
description: Walk-through: under llama-server's grammar, Gemma 4 E4B pads every JSON answer, spending 16 output tokens per Pick instead of 7. That more than doubles decode tokens on the provisional default model, on every Pick and every sample, while decode already takes 106-430 ms per Pick on 4B Vulkan. Compact whitespace exists only as a per-model choice that has not yet been measured.
evidence: doc 55 TL;DR and §6.2 (16 vs 7 tokens); agent-runtime §16 item 8 (doc 46 OQ5); doc 51 §4.3 (compact whitespace is a preset choice); doc 53 §3 (decode times).
frequency: constant: every Pick and Fill on Gemma-family local setups
removal: Make the wrong input impossible. Local grammars for Pick and Fill in the general fallback preset forbid optional whitespace, which yields compact JSON by construction. Check on the tuning split that accuracy does not drop before shipping; the check is required.
change_in: doc 55 default preset; doc 51 §4.4; agent-runtime §3; plotroom-provider-http

title: Over-large MCP results return only their size, and error text names tools that do not exist
description: Walk-through: an external agent asks for all units in a large mission and gets back only the result's size (doc 56 PK3). It has to guess a narrower filter and call again, spending a round trip with no data. Doc 57's TM1 envelope, designed for Wilco and plugins, would return a capped first page, the exact omitted count, a cursor and a narrowing hint instead. Repair text such as 'call list_commands for valid ids' names a tool that is not in the manifest.
evidence: doc 56 PK3 ('an over-large result returns its size instead'), PK2; doc 57 §5.2 TM1, TE-G9; doc 61 §4.5 (result card); commands-undo-history §3 (list_commands).
frequency: workflow: large queries and argument errors over MCP
removal: Make the wrong input impossible, which also removes the extra call. Use one envelope (TM1) for Wilco, plugins and MCP: a capped first page, shown and total counts, a cursor, and a narrowing hint that names real filter fields; the hidden list and depth cap stay. Every error's repair text names only tools in that client's manifest, enforced by the PK2 check (shared with FR-M-018).
change_in: doc 56 PK3; doc 57 TM1; commands-undo-history §3; extensibility §10; plotroom-mcp

title: Errors that name no fix, and prompts that show a same-named item with another shape, stall weak models' repairs
area: model-facing: diagnostics and findings without a next action
description: In doc 64's pilot (three 3-4B local models writing Rust against an unseen API) the models called a unit enum variant with a payload (`Refusal::OutOfMap(label)`), a form the prompt itself showed: the same listing has `Problem::OutOfMap(String)`. rustc's E0618 ('expected function, found `Refusal`') names no fix, and it was cleared in 9 of 318 repair transitions, against 11 of 28 for errors with a custom fix note and 55 of 189 for rustc's own `?` notes that name the missing `From` impl [descriptive, and confounded by the name collision]. The same pattern appears wherever a check reports a problem without the next action: Teller findings, validator messages, tool errors for Wilco and external agents [I].
evidence: doc 64 §4.4 item 1 and §4.5 (pilot records, 2026-09-28); tools/rust-weak-models/crates/mb-spec/src/refusal.rs; doc 61 §4.6 item 5; doc 62 §3.1
frequency: constant: every repair turn that meets such a finding
removal: Make the wrong input impossible first: no same-named items with different shapes in anything shown to a model, and types shaped so the likely guess is correct (doc 64 P64-S3). Where a hint-less error remains, the checker or harness names the fix: every Teller finding and validator message carries the next action and the allowed values (doc 61 §4.6 item 5), and a harness-side rewrite covers compiler errors no attribute reaches (doc 64 §6 step 12). Measure per-code clearance in the qualification suites so a sticky code shows up (doc 64 P64-W2). Keeps typed findings, validation and the glass box intact. Resolve together with FR-M-031.
change_in: docs/research/61-language-service-for-the-llm.md §4.6; Teller's finding catalog; the plugin SDK's LLM_CONTEXT.md (doc 62 §7); tools/rust-weak-models (spec fix, doc 64 §6 step 2); qualification suites (docs 44, 48)

title: Tests, the most informative feedback, are out of reach while a whole file fails to compile
area: model-facing: task shape for coding steps
description: In doc 64's pilot only 12 of 806 rounds compiled, so the visible tests ran in 12 rounds and their failures were fed back in 3. Generation took 97.7% of the recorded time and cargo 2.3%, so the cost was not compilation but never getting past it. Any loop that hands a weak model a whole file (a plugin, a script) and feeds back only the first failing phase has the same shape [I].
evidence: doc 64 §4.9 (time split from the pilot records; tools/rust-weak-models/analysis/time_split.py); doc 64 §3.9 (unit-sized shape)
frequency: workflow: every weak-model coding task of file size
removal: Eliminate the step size that causes it: give weak models unit-sized work, one function against a compiling skeleton with that function's tests as spec and feedback (doc 64 §3.9, P64-S6), once DR9-DR12b show it helps; for Wilco and scripts only as an input to D051's qualification, never a default. Until then every run summary reports the share of rounds that reach the tests. Keeps the same checks and the verifier loop.
change_in: tools/rust-weak-models (unit-sized shape, doc 64 §6 step 5); the plugin SDK scaffold (doc 62 §7); doc 65 §6

title: In a clippy loop, weak models fail compiling rounds on unused imports and meet lint follow-ups that carry no custom text
area: model-facing: lint feedback in repair loops
description: Under `-D warnings` an unused import fails a round: 11 of doc 64's 12 compiling pilot rounds carried a rustc warning, and 404 of 434 warning headings in the saved feedback were unused imports. rustc's help for a `must_use` error suggests `let _ = ...`, which then fails clippy's `let_underscore_must_use` with only 'consider explicitly using expression value', and an `allow` or `expect` under a module-level `forbid` fails with E0453 ('incompatible with previous forbid'); neither names the sanctioned API (probed with rustc 1.98.1 and clippy 0.1.98). Strong agents fix these in one line; weak models spend repair rounds on them [I].
evidence: doc 64 §4.9 and §3.9 (lint arm, interaction items 1-4; probe notes in its verification notes); AGENTS.md 'Fast inner loop, full gates at the end' and 'Diagnostics as Guidance'
frequency: workflow: every weak-model repair loop that runs clippy with deny-level lints
removal: Choose a safe default for weak-model loops: warnings fed back after errors without failing the round, deny-level lints at the final gate (doc 64 DR14 decides with data); `must_use` messages that name the sanctioned use; a scaffold that says its lint levels are fixed. The rules for strong coding agents in AGENTS.md stay as they are, and the full gates at the end stay intact.
change_in: the plugin SDK scaffold and LLM_CONTEXT.md (doc 62 §7; doc 64 P64-S5, P64-S6); contributor guidance for weak-model loops; tools/rust-weak-models (GUIDED-L arm)

title: API surfaces invite wrong guesses: a `?` that cannot convert at the boundary, and fallible and infallible steps with no naming cue
area: model-facing: API shape for generated code
description: The most frequent E0277 in both arms of doc 64's pilot was '`?` couldn't convert the error to `Refusal`': models applied `?` to library results inside a function that returns another error type. Under the typestate API, 134 saved feedback blocks (Qwen 14, Gemma 16, Granite 104, many of Granite's repeats) said `?` can only be applied to values that implement `Try`, because the models put `?` on steps that return a value directly; the plain API had 20, all Granite's. A surface that mixes fallible and infallible steps without a cue invites the guess that every step is fallible [I].
evidence: doc 64 §4.4 item 2 and §4.6 (pilot records, 2026-09-28); doc 64 P64-S3
frequency: constant: every generated step that crosses the API boundary
removal: Make the likely guess correct: library errors convert into the caller's result type with `?` (`From` impls); builder steps are either all fallible or visibly named; result enums have one construction shape (doc 64 P64-S3). Applies to the plugin SDK and any Rust surface agents write against. Keeps typed errors intact. Resolve together with FR-M-028.
change_in: the plugin SDK (doc 62 §7); AGENTS.md 'Diagnostics as Guidance' only if doc 64's Stage 1 supports it

title: AGENTS.md rule load: over 700 lines auto-loaded into every session, mostly prose rules for code that does not exist yet
description: CLAUDE.md is a one-line include of AGENTS.md, so every agent session pays about 40 KB (~10k tokens) before its first read (about 47 KB on re-check later on 2026-09-28). That includes docs-only and tools-only sessions, which is all the work so far. Lines 248-679 (~60%) were Rust coding rules ('Coding Session Discipline') for crates that do not exist yet; on re-check later on 2026-09-28 they are lines 248-782 (~66%). The file breaks its own ~600-line soft ceiling. Many rules could be checked mechanically (indexing, unwrap, lifetime names, exhaustive matching, doc comments, documented suppressions, file size), but they are written as prose, so compliance depends on an agent reading and remembering them. Doc 62 §8 proposed adding 116 more lines of prose, and on re-check later on 2026-09-28 the working-tree AGENTS.md already carries that text ('Diagnostics as Guidance', 'Negative Compile Tests', the witness and guard rules). Some rules have no scope: 'Every problem, issue, or bug fixed must include a regression test and additional security/vulnerability tests' reads as if it also covers doc fixes, and 'Build: cargo build' is listed and then banned.
evidence: AGENTS.md (712 lines, 40,105 bytes when swept; 816 lines, 46,758 bytes on re-check later on 2026-09-28); CLAUDE.md = '@AGENTS.md'; AGENTS.md §4 '~600 lines is the soft ceiling'; AGENTS.md 'Coding Session Discipline' (lines 248-679 when swept; 248-782 on re-check); AGENTS.md 'Local Repo-Specific Rules' (build listed, then forbidden); CODE-INDEX §1 'read it first, always'; doc 62 §5.3 (table mapping AGENTS.md prose rules to existing lints: single_char_lifetime_names, wildcard_enum_match_arm, missing_docs, allow_attributes_without_reason, too_many_lines) and §8 (+116 lines; its heading still reads 'awaiting owner approval', although the text is in the working-tree AGENTS.md on re-check); crate-map §2.4 (planned clippy deny set); decisions/README ('records that restate an AGENTS.md invariant summarise it').
frequency: session: every agent session
removal: Make wrong input impossible, then eliminate. (1) Move mechanically checkable rules into workspace lints, clippy.toml (with instruction-style reasons) and xtask checks (doc 62 §5.3), leaving one line each. (2) Move the Rust coding, testing and allocation rules (about 430 lines when swept, about 535 on re-check) into a topic file loaded when touching code: for Claude Code a nested CLAUDE.md that includes it under the future crates/ directory; Codex uses nested AGENTS.md files. (3) Keep the product invariants (agent product scope, campaign-first harness, glass box, friction review), hygiene and naming sections in full in the always-loaded core; they were about 110 lines when swept (about 150 on re-check, with the Friction Review section), the decisions README treats AGENTS.md as the source that D006 and D009-D014 summarise, and shortening them to pointers would move authority and hide concrete prohibitions (no shell, no arbitrary file or network access, plugin rules) from sessions that do not follow the pointer. (4) Give each rule an explicit scope (code, tests, docs, tools), and remove 'Build: cargo build' from the command list. Carry doc 62 §8's rules mainly as lint configuration rather than prose (on re-check its text is already in the working-tree AGENTS.md). Changing AGENTS.md needs the owner.
change_in: AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md; architecture/crate-map.md §2.4; doc 62 §8 amendment; architecture/testing-strategy.md §14

title: docs/README.md, where every reading order starts, is too big for one tool read and hides its rows from search
description: The index is 502 lines but 64 KB (507 lines and 66 KB on re-check the same day). A single Read returns it truncated (26,302 tokens against a 25,000 cap), so an agent told to 'use §4 to pick one record' may never see §5-§8. The 'one line per row' rule makes §5 rows 353-931 characters long, and content search reports them as '[Omitted long matching line]', so a grep-driven agent cannot see which doc covers a topic. The 600-line ceiling is the wrong measure: this file passes it and still cannot be read in one call. The implementer reading order (AGENTS.md, CODE-INDEX, docs/README, the decision index and the DG index) costs about 55k tokens before any topic file.
evidence: docs/README.md (502 lines, 64,307 bytes when swept; 507 lines, 66,141 bytes on re-check; a Read truncated at 26,302 tokens against a 25,000 cap); docs/README lines 287-302 are 353-931 characters (line 290: 931), and Grep prints '[Omitted long matching line]' for them; docs/README §3.2 and §3.3 reading orders; §8 ('if it grows past that, split §5 into docs/research/README.md'); sizes: AGENTS.md 40 KB (47 KB on re-check), CODE-INDEX 34 KB, decisions/README 27 KB, DG README 17 KB, OWNER-QUESTIONS 47 KB.
frequency: session: every coding-agent session; every lookup
removal: Eliminate, then automate. Do the split §8 already foresees now: move the §5 research table to docs/research/README.md and drop the change-log notes (see FR-C-017). Cap each row at one short sentence and leave detail in the doc itself. For index and entry files, replace the line ceiling with a byte or token budget (each file readable in one call, about 40 KB or less), checked by the repo check script (FR-C-014). Keep a 'Start here' of one screen or less at the top.
change_in: docs/README.md; new docs/research/README.md; AGENTS.md §4 (budget metric for index files); CODE-INDEX.md §6

title: Public-hygiene checks are manual searches repeated every session, and the planned CI grep for private names cannot be committed
description: AGENTS.md asks each committer to 'search the change set'. Each doc then records its own ad-hoc search ('Hygiene search ... none were found'). Doc 49's CSV generator had its own local-path guard, but that script is not committed. testing-strategy §14 plans a CI grep for private project names 'Every push', but a committed list of those names would itself publish them. A missed reference in a public repository cannot be taken back, so this is the costliest check to leave to memory.
evidence: AGENTS.md 'Public Repository Hygiene' last bullet; doc 49 verification notes ('The script refuses to write if a local path or user name appears'; 'Hygiene search. No local paths, user names or private project names were found'); docs/README note 'Links and hygiene review (2026-09-27)'; testing-strategy §14 row 'Public-hygiene grep: ... private project names | Every push'; tools/ holds no check script.
frequency: constant: every commit
removal: Automate. Commit a generic check (drive-letter and home-directory paths, the local user name read at run time, e-mail addresses, key-like strings) as part of the repo check dispatcher (FR-C-014) and an optional pre-commit hook. For private names, prefer a git-ignored pattern file under /private/ locally plus a CI secret for the server-side run, with matches reported without echoing the pattern, so no name ever appears in the tree; a committed salted-hash denylist of a few short names can be brute-forced with a dictionary and is only a weaker fallback. File a DG for testing-strategy §14's private-names row, because it cannot work as written.
change_in: AGENTS.md 'Public Repository Hygiene'; architecture/testing-strategy.md §14; roadmap m0-m3 M0 CI scope; new check script under tools/; new DG

title: New measurement instruments live in scratch copies outside the tree; committed tooling lags and results cannot be reproduced from the repo
description: Long runs read tools/local-qual from the working tree, so docs 53, 55 and 59 build their instruments (letter-probability scoring, --preset, per-field Fill, cascade replay) 'on a scratch copy ... never in the tree while doc 49 uses it'. The doc 48 cloud-backend patch is still listed as 'pending', although OWQ-27 said it lands after doc 49's run and doc 49 is done. The scripts that generated committed CSVs (doc 49) are not committed, and neither are the reviewers' re-derivation scripts. local-qual has no unit tests (quota-sim has 31), so each review re-implements the scoring by hand. Per-model presets (D048) will be tuned on numbers that cannot be regenerated from the repository, and qualification badges and presets rest on these numbers. Doc 64's instrument is the exception: it lives in tools/rust-weak-models with unit tests and pinned prompt hashes, but its run records stay local, so its pilot numbers cannot be re-derived from the repository until a per-episode results CSV lands (doc 64 §6 step 11).

Exists only in a scratch copy of the tooling ... not in the tree' and its tooling bullet (--preset on a scratch copy); doc 59 §6.1 and its note that the --why change 'belongs in the scratch copy'; CODE-INDEX §2 and docs/README §6.4 ('pending patch'); OWQ-27 answer; doc 49 verification notes ('generated by script', 'The reviewer's own scripts re-derived'); tools/local-qual has no test file; tools/quota-sim/test_quota_sim.py.; tools/rust-weak-models (README, test_rwm.py, test_rwm_guards.py); doc 64 §6 step 11

The runner snapshots its own code and suites at start (copies them next to the results and records their hashes, as suite_sha already does for suites), or each long run uses its own git worktree, so development continues in the tree. Commit every generator next to the CSV it produces. Turn the re-derivation checks into unit tests over a stub backend (pick-hard's one-off stub check shows how). Land a pending patch in the same change set that finishes the run that blocked it.

description: AGENTS.md 'Local Repo-Specific Rules' lists cargo build/test/clippy/fmt, but there is no Cargo.toml, so all of them fail. Today's work is docs, CSVs and Python tools. description: Tuning a model's preset (doc 55 section 4) runs arms against an incumbent preset. title: Root-level Cargo, rustup and rustfmt configuration is off-limits while a standalone research workspace sits below the repository root
description: The usual root files would also reach tools/rust-weak-models, a standalone research workspace (doc 64) whose test_rwm.EnclosingWorkspace fails on a root rust-toolchain file or .cargo/config and whose README asks for its own clippy.toml and rustfmt.toml. So the M0 skeleton has no `cargo xtask` alias (it needs [alias] in .cargo/config.toml): contributors type `cargo run -p xtask -- layers`, and coding agents, who may not use `cargo run`, reach the checks only through `cargo test -p xtask` (xtask/tests/live_workspace.rs). The root clippy.toml also applies when someone runs clippy inside the research workspace [I: from that workspace's README, which says clippy reads the nearest clippy.toml above a crate].
